artigo.texto: Mercado global de coletores de calha parabólica: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Mercado global de coletores de calha parabólica deve se expandir até 2035, impulsionado pela demanda por armazenamento de energia térmica Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de Coletores de Calha Parabólica, o mercado inicia 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de coletores de calha parabólica (PTC, na sigla em inglês) entra em uma fase de renovada importância estratégica, à medida que os sistemas de energia priorizam capacidade renovável despachável. Diferentemente dos sistemas fotovoltaicos, os coletores de calha parabólica integram armazenamento de energia térmica de custo competitivo, o que permite gerar eletricidade ou fornecer calor industrial além das horas de luz solar. Este relatório analisa o mercado de 2026 a 2035, abrangendo conjuntos completos de coletores, espelhos, tubos receptores, estruturas de suporte e sistemas de rastreamento. A análise identifica as usinas CSP de escala utilitária como o principal uso final, enquanto o calor de processo industrial, o aquecimento distrital, a dessalinização e a recuperação avançada de petróleo oferecem caminhos de diversificação. O cenário competitivo reúne empresas de engenharia consolidadas e fabricantes especializados de componentes. A dinâmica regional é moldada pela qualidade do recurso solar, pelo apoio de políticas públicas e pelas capacidades de fabricação locais. O cenário-base da previsão pressupõe continuidade moderada das políticas, queda dos custos tecnológicos e reconhecimento crescente do valor do armazenamento de longa duração. Os principais riscos incluem a concorrência de sistemas fotovoltaicos com baterias, atrasos no licenciamento e concentração da cadeia de suprimentos. O relatório oferece uma perspectiva baseada em dados para fabricantes, empreiteiras EPC, investidores e formuladores de políticas que atuam nesse mercado em evolução. O cenário-base para o mercado de coletores de calha parabólica de 2026 a 2035 prevê uma expansão moderada, porém constante, com taxa de crescimento anual composta de 4,2% em termos reais. Essa perspectiva se ancora na proposta de valor singular dos coletores de calha parabólica: a capacidade de armazenar energia térmica em escala, oferecendo eletricidade e calor despacháveis que complementam as fontes renováveis variáveis. O crescimento da demanda não repetirá o boom impulsionado por subsídios da década de 2010; será movido, isso sim, por projetos integrados de energia, configurações híbridas e mandatos de descarbonização industrial. As usinas CSP de escala utilitária continuarão sendo o maior segmento, mas sua participação diminuirá gradualmente à medida que as aplicações de calor de processo industrial e aquecimento distrital ganharem tração. Avanços tecnológicos, como receptores de maior temperatura e sistemas avançados de sais fundidos, aumentarão a eficiência e reduzirão o custo nivelado. Restrições na cadeia de suprimentos de componentes especializados, como tubos receptores evacuados, podem moderar o crescimento em determinados anos. Geograficamente, Oriente Médio e África, junto com a Ásia-Pacífico, responderão pela maior parte das novas adições de capacidade, apoiadas por planos nacionais de diversificação energética. América do Norte e Europa terão implantação seletiva, muitas vezes vinculada a projetos de pesquisa ou híbridos. O índice de mercado, com 2025 como ano-base em 100, deve alcançar 151 até 2035, refletindo o crescimento acumulado. Esse cenário-base pressupõe ausência de reversões políticas relevantes e queda gradual dos custos de capital, em linha com as curvas de aprendizado históricas. Vetores e Restrições da Demanda Principais Vetores de Demanda - Crescimento da demanda por energia renovável despachável, impulsionado por requisitos de estabilidade da rede e pela integração de geração solar e eólica variável. - Adoção crescente de soluções de calor de processo industrial, à medida que os fabricantes buscam descarbonizar a produção de vapor em alta temperatura. - Políticas e incentivos governamentais de apoio à implantação de energia solar concentrada, incluindo leilões e créditos fiscais em regiões de cinturão solar. - Redução de custos na integração do armazenamento de energia térmica, ampliando a competitividade econômica dos sistemas de calha parabólica. - Expansão de projetos híbridos solar-gás e solar-dessalinização, sobretudo no Oriente Médio e no Norte da África. - Foco crescente no armazenamento de energia de longa duração para viabilizar o fornecimento renovável ininterrupto. Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Concorrência intensa de sistemas fotovoltaicos com armazenamento em baterias, que registraram rápida queda de custos e prazos de implantação mais curtos. - Altos custos de capital iniciais e longos prazos de desenvolvimento das usinas CSP de escala utilitária, o que desestimula parte dos investidores. - Disponibilidade limitada de componentes especializados, como tubos receptores evacuados, criando gargalos na cadeia de suprimentos. - Incerteza regulatória e mecanismos de apoio inconsistentes em mercados-chave, afetando os pipelines de projetos. - Consumo de água para resfriamento nas usinas CSP convencionais, uma restrição em regiões áridas com escassez hídrica. artigo.texto: Once upon a time in the high-stakes world of clean energy procurement, a project team sat around a conference table, staring at a massive, complex document: the Energy Storage Contract Alliance (ESCA) Model Supply and Purchase Agreement. To the untrained eye, a utility-scale battery contract looks like a dry maze of legal jargon.But to the lead developer and the chief technical officer, this wasn't just paper. It was the superhero blueprint that turned a chaotic market into an accessible, bulletproof project. This is the problem that is sought to be solved with a model BESS contract from ESCA. Buyers representing 40 GWh of utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) projects have launched the Energy Storage Contract Alliance (ESCA) and published an open model contract for buying utility-scale BESS. The contract is meant as a common reference for developers, EPCs, independent power producers, asset owners, and battery manufacturers and integrators. ESCA's twenty-two members are utilities, independent power producers, project developers and asset owners with projects worldwide, including Goldbeck Solar, Neoen, ILOS, Pacifico Energy and Eiffage. Anyone, buyer or supplier, can read the core contract free of charge. Members get the full agreement and its technical appendices. The market is growing fast. Global BESS shipments rose about 75% to around 420 GWh in 2025, and InfoLink Consulting expects around 600 GWh in 2026. Contract terms have not kept up. Many projects still start from a blank page or from one party's own template, and topics such as cell traceability, serial defects, inspection sampling and cybersecurity are handled unevenly. A common reference draft can cut drafting time and transaction costs for both sides and make offers easier to compare. A public baseline also lets suppliers respond to tenders against known requirements, and lets smaller developers negotiate on the same footing as large utilities. "Every BESS project works through the same technical and contractual questions, and most of the answers are not project-specific," said Arthur Claire, Secretary General of ESCA. "Those answers used to stay in each company's drawer. ESCA puts a complete baseline in the open, so any developer, utility or manufacturer can take it, use the parts that fit and ignore the rest." The model contract covers technical specifications, factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning, warranties, payment and price-adjustment mechanisms, and cybersecurity. More than fifteen technical appendices set out requirements at system, rack, pack and cell level. The contract sets no prices, price levels or discounts. These remain entirely for each buyer and supplier to negotiate. Sinovoltaics, ESCA's technical secretariat, drafted the first version as a baseline for members to build on. Users can adopt it in full, in part or not at all, and can change any clause. Members can comment on each clause, and the Steering Committee decides on revisions. The Steering Committee includes MN8 Energy, Neoen, Fortum and Munich RE. "As the energy storage sector is witnessing increasingly large procurement processes that often focus on the lowest possible costs, this race-to-the-bottom approach may undercut vital contractual and procurement-related practices and threaten the viability of a BESS project," commented Naim El Chami, Battery Technical Expert at Neoen and a member of the ESCA Steering Committee. Here is how the ESCA model agreement turns confusing legal hurdles into pure peace of mind for energy buyers. For the full contract, see end of story. Act I: The Shield of Traceability and Quality In years past, buying a massive battery system meant placing an order and praying that the manufacturer didn’t swap out high-grade components for cheaper alternatives halfway through production. Enter Clause 4.3 (The Designated Cell) and Clause 4.5 (Traceability Requirements). The contract acts as a digital ledger that locks down the exact cell chemistry, model, and physical factory site down to the individual serial number. When the CTO's team wants to know where their hardware came from, they don’t get vague promises but a transparent, machine-readable as-built register linking every single container directly to its manufacturing batch. Even better, Clause 4.4 (Change Control) guarantees that the supplier can’t change so much as a line of firmware or a bracket on the enclosure without the buyer’s written blessing. For buyers, this turns what used to be a nerve-wracking "black box" into a crystal-clear glass house. Act II: The Gift of Total Data Visibility (Or, How Buyers Can Stop Worrying and Love the Telemetry) Fast forward to Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT). Normally, a buyer receives a summary PDF signed by the factory manager saying, "Trust us, it passed." Not under this agreement. Clause 5.1.8 and Clause 6.6 (Data Monitoring) hand the keys to the kingdom over to the buyer. The contract mandates 1-second interval raw data streams covering voltage, current, and temperature for every single cell during testing and operation. Through Clause 6.5 (Battery Analytics Solutions), independent software monitors the battery's health in real time. The contract explicitly states that the buyer owns all generated data, can access it without paying hidden subscription fees, and never has to rely on the vendor's cloud servers just to check if their asset is running safely. It makes world-class quality control as accessible and simple as checking a smartphone app. Act III: The Guarantee That Keeps on Giving (Or, The 15-Year Safety Net) As the project approaches commercial operation, the financial team usually asks the scariest question of all: "What happens five or ten years from now when these cells degrade or a component breaks?" This is where the ESCA agreement shows its true beauty through a stacked defense of buyer-friendly guarantees: - The Single Point of Responsibility (Clause 7.1.4): The seller can’t point fingers

artigo.texto: Global law firm Dentons has advised PPF banka a.s. in connection with the financing of the construction and development of the 72 MW BESS Frasinet 1 battery energy storage system project in Romania. With this transaction, PPF banka a.s. has financed a third BESS project of the RSJ PE SF Batteries fund, a joint platform of RSJ Investments and Second Foundation that is building a broader portfolio of battery energy storage assets across the EU. Dentons advised on the drafting and negotiation of the financing and security documentation, reviewed key project contracts, and supported the transaction through to signing and completion, including the issuance of a legal opinion and management of conditions precedent. The cross-border Dentons team included Daniel Hurych, Partner and Co-Head of the Banking and Finance group in Prague, Martin Fiala, Senior Associate, Jan Kořistka, Associate, and Tomáš Husička, Junior Associate, together with Petr Zákoucký, Partner and Head of the Energy practice in Prague. Romanian law advice was provided by a Bucharest-based team comprising Simona Marin, Partner, Stefi Ionescu, Counsel, and Maria Brinza, Associate, all in the Banking and Finance group; Angelica Pintilie, Counsel, Alin Dimache and Carolina Mitea, Associates, all in the Energy group; and Luiza Onofrei, Counsel, and Alice Neagu, Associate, both in the Real Estate group. Dentons said this mandate highlights its capabilities in cross-border project finance and energy infrastructure, combining Czech and Romanian financing, security, real estate, and energy advice to support the development of battery energy storage capacity in Romania.

artigo.texto: Danville has added more than 100 housing units to its market since 2023, with over 200 more in construction. In Pittsylvania, a master-planned community will soon add more than 1,800 units to the county’s housing stock. It’s still not enough, local officials say. Danville and Pittsylvania County are experiencing unprecedented levels of growth, for which the housing market wasn’t prepared. Job creation in the region, which is driving the increase in demand for housing, has picked up rapidly in recent years, after decades of job losses tied to the declining tobacco and textile industries. Large facilities locating at industrial parks in the region are expected to create thousands of jobs in the coming years. The Berry Hill megasite, the largest industrial site in the state, will soon be home to lithium-ion battery separator manufacturer Microporous. Microporous has promised to create about 2,000 new jobs. And data center developer Stack Infrastructure is promising about 2,500 permanent jobs at an AI data center facility that is also expected to come to the Berry Hill site, though there has been no formal announcement. Close to 1,000 new housing units are needed to support the Microporous project alone, according to the Danville Housing Navigator. The workers will need places to live, said Linda Green, executive director of the Southern Virginia Regional Alliance, a regional economic development group. That’s why local development group Southside Investing is building a massive master-planned community development in Axton, nine miles from the megasite. Tony Salah, with Southside Investing, said the group “has been actively preparing to meet the housing demand of future jobs.” The 590-acre development, called Sugar Tree Living, will create more than 1,800 units across all housing types — single-family, apartments, townhomes and senior living. Salah joined other developers, along with real estate professionals, builders, bankers and economic development officials in Danville on Thursday for the fifth annual Southern Virginia Regional Housing Summit. At the event, Green said that housing demand in the region has increased even since 2022, when a study identified a pent-up demand for about 600 single-family homes and 700 apartment units in Danville. “Housing has been built, new projects have been announced and our economic development pipeline has changed substantially,” she said. “But the projections for tomorrow change even faster and more drastically.” Since the study was released, the city has built 112 rental units and 16 for-sale units, with 233 more units in construction. Despite this, the demand has continued to grow, according to a 2025 update to the study. Pent-up demand in the city now calls for nearly 4,000 rental units and 1,300 owned units, said Susan McCulloch, Danville’s director of housing and development. Housing is now seen as a key part of economic development, Green said. Companies always ask about housing when considering whether to locate in an area, she said. “They’re going to ask the housing question, and if you don’t have a solution for it, you can’t win the project,” Green said. “That’s why we increasingly view housing as workforce and economic development infrastructure. You no longer see a division between the departments.” Salah echoed this sentiment, calling the housing deficit “the overwhelming regional refrain of need.” The Pittsylvania County Board of Supervisors approved the Sugar Tree Living project in 2023, over a year before the Microporous announcement, anticipating that a major housing development would be needed to support eventual jobs at the megasite. On top of 1,800 housing units, the development will also offer amenities like healthcare, childcare, retail, dining, hospitality and recreation, and services like on-site fire and rescue. When it was approved, the master-planned community drew some pushback from residents about traffic, loss of agricultural land and the natural beauty of the county, and the possibility that the development could kickstart a chain of similar developments. Microporous locating at the megasite “validated our time and energy and dollars into this area,” Salah said in a 2024 interview after the company’s announcement. “We want to be the supply solution for a portion of the housing demand,” he said then. After Thursday’s housing summit, Salah added that Southside Investing is feeling “more and more confident that an abundant wave of well-paying, good jobs are closer than ever.” A second tenant at the megasite — and thousands of additional jobs — is on the horizon, with data center developer Stack Infrastructure planning to build an AI data center campus on nearly 3,000 acres at the site. A local performance agreement for the project outlines Stack’s promise of $1.3 billion in investment and more than 2,000 permanent jobs. “The housing implication is clear,” Green said. “We must prepare for both permanent employment growth and the workforce needed to construct and equip these growing facilities.” Information about the region’s housing needs, current projects and available sites can be found on the Danville Housing Navigator website.

artigo.texto: Swatara Township approves community benefits plan for data center projects DAUPHIN COUNTY, Pa. (WHP) — Swatara Township's Board of Commissioners approved community benefits agreements for a pair of proposed data centers last week. The agreements include $84.15 million in contributions associated with Highlands West and $36.15 million associated with Highlands East, according to the board. artigo.texto: Peugeot has revived the RCZ nameplate with the RCZ Vision concept car, showcasing the brand’s new design language for a coupé based on the STLA One platform, featuring a solid-state battery and a 1,000-volt electrical architecture. The RCZ Vision concept’s powertrain is claimed to output 500 hp and deliver up to 600 km of range with a claimed energy consumption figure of 11.5 kWh per 100 km, and its solid-state battery is said to to be able to be recharged from 10-80% in just 10 minutes, according to Peugeot. The RCZ Vision concept is Peugeot’s first expression of its “Feline Future” direction that will inform the design of future Peugeot models. According to Autocar, the RCZ Vision concept measures 4.65 m long, 1.35 m tall and 1.94 m wide, while its rolling stock is a set of forged aluminium wheels measuring 21 inches and 22 inches in diameter front and rear, respectively. Its cabin is designed to be a true four-seater, rather than the 2+2 configuration of its discontinued production namesake, and the RCZ Vision concept aims to accommodate two adults comfortably in the second row. The double-bubble roof of the previous RCZ has been rethought to optimise rear-seat headroom, while adding light to the cabin. Further maximising interior space is the RCZ Vision’s battery, which measures just 110 mm thick in order to retain a low floor and low-profile silhouette. Practicality and usability were priorities for the design team when designing the new RCZ Vision, as to maximise the likelihood of the car being adapted to production, said Peugeot design director Matthias Hossann. “This was an important part of my brief. I asked my team to make it look quite realistic in terms of proportion and size, in order to make this car more approachable. It’s not just designing a UFO or something which is highly futuristic,” Hossann told the publication. Inside, the cabin of the RCZ Vision concept is installed with the Hypersquare steering “wheel” that first featured on the Polygon concept, and the rectangular steering “wheel” will feature in the next-generation e-208. Displays in the RCZ Vision concept are transparent displays rather than traditional screens, which Peugeot says enables the driver to configure the information displayed, and the central display can even be completely switched off, where the transparent screen offers cleaner aesthetic. This setup of transparent displays complements the Hypersquare “wheel”, which offers access to main functions via the four rings close to hand, and therefore does not require the driver to move their hands from the steering control, says Peugeot. The RCZ Vision concept also serves to showcase the French manufacturer’s “X-by-wire” technologies including steer-by-wire, which means that it does not have a physical connection between the steering and the steered wheels. Peugeot says that steer-by-wire enables the use of variable ratio steering, such as to offer much quicker input at low vehicle speeds and reduced ratios for more stable steering when the vehicle is travelling at higher speeds. Also taking the by-wire approach is the braking system in the RCZ Vision, and the system is said to offer more precise braking modulation and seamless integration of regenerative braking. For ADAS, the RCZ Vision gets “Level 2++” automation, according to Peugeot.

artigo.texto: Key Capture Energy NY1 at Luther Forest in Saratoga County was the first utility-scale battery energy storage system in New York. It is located in Stillwater and broke ground in 2018. HUDSON— The Common Council’s legal committee recommended a six-month pause on battery energy storage systems in the city at a meeting Thursday. The move means the full council will vote on the proposal at its next meeting. The energy storage systems store power, typically from renewable sources, in rechargeable batteries for later use. Common Council President Margaret Morris said the moratorium recommendation began after developers reached out about building the facilities in Hudson. “Our code enforcement officer (Nick Fox) reached out to me, and he had had a couple of inquiries from, I think, two companies inquiring about what Hudson has in its code in relation to large-scale battery operations,” Morris said. One company is eyeing the site of the former Overhead Door garage building on Hudson Avenue, Morris said. Because Hudson has nothing in its code regarding the facilities, Fox suggested the council take some action. The council should be careful not to regulate an opportunity to bring revenue to the city, support the electrical grid, and help the environment, 3rd Ward Councilmember Jason Foster said. Morris countered that battery storage systems are mostly large-scale operations, not compatible with a two-square-mile city like Hudson, and compared them to artificial-intelligence data centers. Morris also cited the risk of large battery fires that can last for weeks, a concern that has led to moratoriums throughout the Twin Counties, including in neighboring Claverack. “There is benefit to these if they didn't catch on fire and didn't explode,” Foster said. “That is always possible. But they are balancing out the grid… I'm just trying to think about ways to help our budget and discuss it further rather than going straight to ixnay.” While the fire risk is concerning, the area does need to be developed, 4th Ward Councilmember Jennifer Belton said. “I would frankly rather see some other kind of small industry come in and do something in that same space,” Belton said. The Columbia Economic Development Corporation has made multiple attempts to get the current owners to sell the property, Morris said. With so much uncertainty, the smartest move would be to pass a moratorium on facilities while city lawmakers reach an agreement on next steps, Common Council attorney Ken Dow said. “If there's not a consensus about just prohibiting them or limiting places where they could go, I think it would be prudent to do a local law, instituting a moratorium for 3 to 6 months,” Dow said. “That way nothing gets in there that you regret. You can then figure out in more detail other places (for the facilities), learn more about these things, the size of them, put together something over the next few months and then modify the code.” Morris said Hudson would use moratoria from other municipalities to shape its moratorium. Foster also asked for an informational presentation on the battery energy storage systems.

artigo.texto: SPARTANBURG —A former cryptocurrency mining facility in the Tiger River Industrial Park is being converted into a data center. The company hopes it’s operational by the end of 2027. BV Power Alpha previously received a fee-in-lieu-of-tax agreement for its crypto mining facility that started up in 2022. The company, owned by Jerry Tang, is now called AIB Data Centers. In February, Tang abandoned efforts to build a new data center in the Tyger River Industrial Park after Spartanburg County Council declined to offer tax incentives in the wake of community criticism over the project. Since then, county council passed a data center moratorium that could prevent new data centers that have an IT electrical load of 65 megawatts or more. Council voted to include the caveat after lobbying from William Crawford, president of Pacolet Milliken, and Bryan Stone, president of Pacolet Milliken subsidiary Lockhart Power, who argued that small data centers create revenue that helps keep costs down for ratepayers. Pacolet Milliken developed the Tyger River Industrial Park and Lockhart supplies much of the power there. The new AIB data center will have an electrical load of only 50 megawatts, falling below that 65-megawatt threshold, according to the company. It will buy power from a utility instead of producing it, meaning it won’t create the type of air pollution that the NorthMark data center will generate. Company spokesperson Pierre DuBois said in an email that the planned data center would exist on the same land footprint as the bitcoin mining facility. “Essentially, the same equipment moves inside the walls, with other equipment added within those walls,” he added. DuBois also said the water use in the data center would be a fraction of what the crypto mining facility used. “Since the site began operating, it has used about 14,000 gallons a day,” said DuBois. “We estimate the data center will use about 165 gallons a day.” For comparison, the NorthMark data center projects to use more than 1 million gallons a day. In an email, DuBois said the new data center wouldn’t be a “hyperscale mega-project,” and that the company “offered to give up incentives awarded to the crypto mining facility in 2022, which would otherwise have carried over to the data center. The county accepted.” According to a news release, AIB has already signed a 12-year agreement with Dutch AI company Nebius. It includes two potential five-year renewal periods.

artigo.texto: APsystems to Showcase Advanced C&I Energy Storage Solutions at Smart Energy Forum 2026 PRAGUE, Oct. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- October 14–15, 2026, APsystems will present its latest solar and energy storage solutions at Smart Energy Forum (SEF) 2026, held on October 14-15 at PVA EXPO PRAHA in Letňany, Prague. Visitors are invited to meet the APsystems team at Booth 1-10 and discover a comprehensive portfolio of solutions spanning commercial & industrial energy storage, residential storage, DIY energy storage, and microinverter technologies. As Europe's energy landscape continues to evolve, the integration of solar generation, energy storage, and intelligent energy management is becoming increasingly important. Commercial and industrial customers are seeking energy storage solutions that deliver exceptional safety, long-term reliability, and operational flexibility. These market demands are at the heart of the technologies APsystems will present in Prague. Advanced Liquid-Cooled C&I Energy Storage in Focus Taking center stage at the APsystems booth will be the APstorage 261L and APstorage 2000L, two all-in-one liquid-cooled energy storage systems designed to meet the needs of demanding commercial and industrial projects. The APstorage 261L is a robust industrial-grade solution engineered for challenging environments. It features a four-layer fire protection architecture, IP65-rated battery packs, and a C4/C5 anti-corrosion cabinet for enhanced durability. The system has successfully passed the rigorous UL 9540A fire propagation test, further validating its industry-leading safety performance. Its all-in-one design supports up to ten units in parallel, providing up to 2 MWh of storage capacity, while its compact 1.3 m² footprint and factory pre-assembled configuration can reduce on-site installation time by more than 40%. For larger-scale applications, the APstorage 2000L delivers utility-grade performance with system availability exceeding 99%. Its cluster-level independent management architecture ensures continued operation even in the event of a PCS failure. Equipped with advanced grid-forming capabilities, the system supports black-start functionality and reliable performance in both weak-grid and off-grid environments. It also maintains full-rated output at ambient temperatures of up to 50°C, making it suitable for a wide range of operating conditions. Residential Storage, DIY Solutions and Microinverters In addition to its C&I portfolio, APsystems will showcase the ELT-12 three-phase AC-coupled residential energy storage solution, paired with the APbattery 51.2V / 10.24 kWh battery system. The company will also feature the APB-U-16L, its latest high-capacity 16 kWh battery, providing homeowners with even greater flexibility when designing residential storage systems. Visitors will also have the opportunity to discover Lake-6, a single-phase plug-in AC-coupled energy storage system featuring an integrated 6 kWh battery and 2,500 W charging and discharging power. Designed for simplicity and ease of installation, Lake-6 makes DIY and residential energy storage more accessible than ever. Completing the lineup is the QT2D, APsystems' proven three-phase microinverter solution. Offering module-level monitoring and control, the QT2D combines high efficiency, safety, and intelligent energy management, making it an excellent choice for both residential and commercial solar installations. Meet APsystems in Prague Throughout SEF 2026, APsystems product specialists and sales representatives will be on hand to demonstrate the company's latest technologies, answer technical questions, and discuss project opportunities and potential partnerships. Visitors can also take part in interactive games and activities at the booth for a chance to win exclusive APsystems giveaways while exploring the full range of solutions on display. Visit APsystems at Booth 1-10, PVA EXPO PRAHA, Prague, on October 14-15, 2026. artigo.texto: Sergio Sgobbi — diretor de Relações Institucionais e Governamentais da Brasscom (Associação das Empresas de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação de Tecnologias Digitais) A aprovação do Regime Especial de Tributação para Data Centers (Redata) representa um marco histórico para a política industrial e digital brasileira. O programa cria condições para reduzir os custos de investimento em infraestrutura digital e posicionar o país de forma mais competitiva na nova economia global. No entanto, é preciso falar com franqueza técnica: o Redata, de forma isolada, não soluciona o gargalo da carga tributária sobre os equipamentos de tecnologia da informação (TI) utilizados nos data centers. Fique por dentro das notÃcias que importam para vocÃª! O programa federal suspende a incidência de PIS/Cofins (Programa de Integração Social e Contribuição para o Financiamento da Seguridade Social) e IPI (Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados) é sobre uma lista de equipamentos de tecnologia da informação (TI). Trata-se de uma medida vital em um setor altamente intensivo em capital, no qual servidores e sistemas de armazenamento representam cerca de 70% dos investimentos. Contudo, uma verdade precisa ser dita: o principal peso tributário sobre os equipamentos continua sendo o ICMS (Imposto sobre Circulação de Mercadorias e Serviços). Enquanto o debate público se concentra na desoneração federal, o ICMS responde por dois terços do total da carga tributária. Isso significa que, embora o Redata antecipe um ambiente favorável, o ganho real de competitividade será limitado caso os estados não se unam a esse esforço por meio da aprovação do convênio no Conselho Nacional de Política Fazendária (Confaz), que permite a redução de até 90% do ICMS. A dinâmica é incontornável. Hoje, grandes operadores globais definem seus aportes comparando custos de implantação, matriz energética, segurança jurídica e incentivos tributários. Países disputam esses aportes, pois sabem que atraem inovação, geram empregos, estimulam outros setores e ampliam a capacidade digital de toda a economia. Nesse contexto, diferenças tributárias tornam-se decisivas. Quando um grupo internacional avalia instalar um data center na América Latina, o Brasil concorre com mercados que oferecem condições agressivas. Se o custo de equipamentos permanecer elevado pelo ICMS, perderemos competitividade num momento em que a demanda por infraestrutura digital cresce exponencialmente, impulsionada pela inteligência artificial e processamento em nuvem. Outro ponto que merece destaque é a inteligência estrutural do Redata. A política não se limita a benefícios tributários; ele estabelece mecanismos de habilitação para projetos de investimento e de coabilitação para empresas que fabricam ou comercializam os equipamentos. Esses instrumentos são essenciais, pois, sem eles, corre-se o risco de a desoneração não ser transferida para a economia. O objetivo do programa é assegurar que a redução tributária chegue ao investimento final e, posteriormente, ao consumidor de serviços digitais, ou seja, a verticalização dos benefícios para toda a cadeia. O sucesso do Redata não deve ser medido apenas pelos impostos reduzidos, mas pela capacidade sistêmica de diminuir o custo do processamento e armazenamento de dados. Quanto mais eficiente o processo, maior a competitividade das empresas que dependem da infraestrutura digital globalmente. Vale lembrar que o Brasil é contumaz importador de capacidade computacional, que em 2025 atingiu o deficit de US$ 7,9 bilhões. A implementação do programa precisa avançar. A regulamentação dos instrumentos de habilitação deve ocorrer com rapidez, objetividade e sem travas que desincentivem investimentos. Ao mesmo tempo, é indispensável construir uma agenda federativa com os Estados na estratégia nacional de atração de investimentos. A transformação digital tornou-se pilar do crescimento no século 21. Inteligência artificial, nuvem e economia de dados dependem de infraestrutura robusta. O Brasil possui vantagens, como matriz elétrica limpa e condição geopolítica estável. Mas essas virtudes não serão suficientes se o ambiente tributário onera os investimentos. O Redata é um passo decisivo. Contudo, seu potencial será plenamente alcançado apenas quando União e estados atuarem de forma coordenada. Sem a redução do ICMS, a política ficará incompleta. Com ela, o Brasil terá condições de se consolidar como polo global de infraestrutura, atraindo bilhões, gerando empregos e fortalecendo sua autonomia tecnológica. O desafio agora não é apenas celebrar a conquista. É garantir que ela produza todos os resultados que o país precisa para liderar a economia digital do futuro.

artigo.texto: BYD is studying whether to manufacture lithium batteries in Argentina, Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno said on Thursday after meeting Stella Li, the Chinese electric vehicle maker’s executive vice-president. According to Quirno, the company was looking at “investment opportunities in Argentina linked to the lithium value chain, particularly in the production of batteries and energy storage systems”. He did not say how much BYD might spend or where the factory could go. The minister tied the talks to Argentinian President Javier Milei’s economic agenda, saying Argentina was positioning itself “as a platform for projects aimed at both the domestic market and exports”. Quirno credited the government’s policies with promoting investment and mining in the country. BYD has sold only imported cars in Argentina since it opened for business in October last year, and it has not announced production plans in the country. It sold 10,000 vehicles in August, including a Dolphin Mini in Rosario, and now has 21 dealerships, most of them in Buenos Aires. The company’s local subsidiary, BYD Auto Argentina SAU, registered with the Justice Ministry in August last year with a corporate purpose that already included making vehicles, batteries and auto parts, the South China Morning Post reported at the time. Christian Kimelman, who runs the Argentine operation, said a car factory was not on the table for now. “It is not in the plans, but anyone who knows the Argentine industry knows that, to lead the sector in the current context, you need to have some kind of vision in that direction,” he told Bloomberg Linea earlier this year. Kimelman said most of BYD’s supply for Argentina and Mexico would come from its factory in Camacari, in the Brazilian state of Bahia. The plant opened in October last year with capacity for 150,000 vehicles a year, and in March Li said it had orders for 50,000 cars from each country. Cars made in Brazil can enter Argentina largely duty-free under the automotive agreement between the two Mercosur members. Vehicles from outside the bloc pay a 35 per cent tariff, except for a quota of 50,000 units that Chinese brands have dominated. BYD has also kept shipping cars from China on its own vessels, and in January the BYD Changzhou unloaded more than 5,000 vehicles at the port of Zarate. The company registered 9,266 cars in Argentina in the first half of the year, according to the importers’ chamber. A lithium venture in Argentina would follow BYD’s failed attempt in Chile, where it had planned a US$290 million cathode plant in Antofagasta. The factory was meant to make 50,000 tonnes a year of lithium iron phosphate cathode material, using lithium from SQM at a preferential price. But BYD and Tsingshan, the other Chinese company Chile’s development agency, Corfo, picked for the scheme, both pulled out in May last year. At that time, Corfo blamed the collapse in lithium prices. -- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST

artigo.texto: A joint South Korean research team has announced a finding that could accelerate the commercialization of next-generation lithium-metal batteries: a high-performance electrolyte formulation made entirely from two inexpensive, off-the-shelf solvents that battery researchers had long considered individually unsuitable — and had never thought to combine — tripling cycle life under demanding conditions compared with conventional electrolytes tested in identical circumstances. The result challenges a design principle that has dominated the field for decades. The Battery Chemistry That Could Double EV Range — and Its Long-Standing Problem Lithium-metal batteries have sat just beyond the commercial horizon for the better part of five decades. The appeal is straightforward: swap the graphite anode in today's electric vehicle batteries for lithium metal, and you can theoretically double — and in some research estimates multiply by up to ten times — the energy stored per kilogram. That translates directly into longer driving range without a heavier or larger battery pack, and into cheaper, more compact grid-scale energy storage systems. The obstacle is equally straightforward: lithium metal is exceptionally reactive. Every time a lithium-metal battery charges, the anode reacts with the surrounding liquid electrolyte. Those reactions build up a protective layer called the solid electrolyte interphase, or SEI, on the anode surface. On graphite, this layer forms once and stabilizes. On lithium metal, it cracks, regrows, and thickens with every cycle — consuming lithium and electrolyte irreversibly, promoting the growth of needle-like lithium dendrites that can short-circuit the cell, and triggering destructive side reactions at the cathode. The result is rapid capacity fade. Under the high-voltage conditions required to push maximum energy from a cell, the problem intensifies. The prevailing engineering response has been to use electrolytes that minimize the strength of the solvent's grip on lithium ions. Strongly solvating solvents — those that cluster tightly around a lithium ion in solution — raise the energy barrier for the ion to shed those solvent molecules and deposit as metal on the anode, a step called desolvation. Poor desolvation means uneven plating, which means a bad SEI, which means short cycle life. The conventional fix has been to use either expensive fluorinated solvents that bind lithium more weakly, or to dissolve lithium salts at very high concentrations to push the chemistry in a more favorable direction. Both approaches add manufacturing cost and complexity. An Unexpected Combination The team, led by Professor Song Hyun-kon of the Department of Energy and Chemical Engineering at the Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST) and Professor Seo Dong-hwa of the Department of Materials Science and Engineering at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST), focused instead on two commodity chemicals that the battery field had previously ruled out: ethylene carbonate (EC) and sulfolane (SL). Both researchers are confirmed specialists in battery electrolyte design with a track record of publication in high-impact materials science journals. Both solvents are produced industrially at large scale and are inexpensive. Both had been excluded from lithium-metal battery electrolyte design for the same fundamental reason: they bind to lithium ions too strongly. EC in particular is a workhorse of the conventional lithium-ion battery industry — it is the primary solvent in most EV battery electrolytes today — but it is well-documented as incompatible with lithium metal anodes, where its tight grip on lithium ions and its tendency to decompose continuously at the reactive lithium surface rapidly degrade the cell. Sulfolane, a polar industrial solvent with similarly high binding affinity for lithium, had been studied as a battery solvent on its own and rejected for analogous reasons. What the UNIST–KAIST team found and reported in ACS Nano on August 11, 2026, is that mixing EC and SL at a 3-to-7 weight ratio — together with a lithium salt and a small quantity of an SEI-stabilizing additive — produces an electrolyte that behaves in a way neither solvent predicts individually. What Does 'Cooperative Solvation' Actually Mean? When EC and SL molecules are present together at that ratio, strong intermolecular forces arise between them — specifically, hydrogen bonds between EC's hydrogen atoms and SL's oxygen atoms. These inter-solvent bonds pull the two molecules toward each other rather than toward the lithium ion. The result is counterintuitive: each solvent's individual binding affinity for lithium ions is weakened by the presence of the other. The team called this mechanism cooperative solvation. The mechanism works through the structure of the lithium ion's immediate environment in solution. Normally, a lithium ion in an EC-based electrolyte is surrounded by EC molecules in what is called the first solvation sheath — typically four to six molecules arranged around the ion. When EC and SL are mixed in the cooperative ratio, both solvents appear simultaneously in that first solvation sheath in a new configuration that the team verified through computational modeling. The co-localized solvents effectively share the coordination of the lithium ion, and because they are also coordinating with each other through hydrogen bonding, the total binding energy available for each solvent to hold onto the lithium is reduced. Desolvation — the step where lithium ions must shed their solvent shell before depositing on the anode — becomes easier. "Mixing two strongly binding solvents to actually weaken their interaction with lithium ions represents a new design principle that overturns conventional electrolyte design wisdom," first author Jinki Hong stated in the research announcement. artigo.texto: More than 50 people marched to Ameren Missouri’s St. Louis headquarters Saturday to speak out against the company’s newly published plans to build more fossil fuel resources in the coming 20 years. The group wore nature-inspired costumes while holding signs calling for clean energy. The People’s Joy Parade and the Sierra Club organized the demonstration with speakers from Tenants Transforming St. Louis, the Missouri Coalition for the Environment and Labadie Environmental Organization. “We can create the clean energy future that we need. We can create it through people power, through love of our communities, and through good organizing,” said Jenn DeRose, the Sierra Club’s campaign organizing strategist for Beyond Coal in Missouri. She stressed the need to develop energy sources like solar and wind power with battery storage to make it available around the clock. Ameren Missouri recently released a new long-range plan that would significantly increase the amount of power plants in its portfolio to meet growing demand for electricity. The company said that growth is primarily driven by new large data centers moving to Missouri. The new resource plan increases the number of new natural gas power plants to nine while also extending the lives of two existing coal plants. Both resources emit planet-warming gases that contribute to climate change. Patricia Schuba lives near the Labadie Coal Plant, which will now operate all four of its units until 2042, rather than shuttering two units in 2036. The plant is about 35 miles west of St. Louis on the Missouri River. Schuba and other demonstrators hit a Labadie power plant piñata that was filled with candy made to look like coal. She said she is not normally that kind of person but feels “righteous rage” about the plans to keep the plant that she said has made her and her neighbors sick open longer. “We approached the solution in a peaceful way, but we need to express that we are very angry with these decisions,” Schuba said. “The people sitting in the building behind me make those decisions every day for all of us, for our children, for future generations, and we need to hold them accountable.” Ameren Missouri executive Ajay Arora told St. Louis Public Radio in September that keeping Labadie operating longer would save customers money. “Labadie remains one of the most affordable plants in the country and recognizing the economic conditions for all our customers and how important reliability and affordability is, that's really factored into delaying the retirement of a few of the Labadie units by a few years,” Arora said. On Saturday, the protesters said electricity is not affordable in the St. Louis region and condemned Ameren’s practice of disconnecting customers who are behind on their bills. “They say they care about affordability and that they're here to serve us. Is that true?” Sarah Watkins, an organizer with Tenants Transforming St. Louis, asked the crowd. “If Ameren cares so much about us, then why are tens of thousands of families losing their electricity every year?” Bills could rise again soon as Ameren is asking Missouri regulators to approve a rate increase for customers. Both the proposed rate increase and the new integrated resource plan are subject to approval by Missouri’s Public Service Commission.

artigo.texto: As the global transition toward renewable energy accelerates, the race to capture market share in storage and delivery is intensifying. Deciding between Eos Energy Enterprises (EOSE -5.16%) and Plug Power (PLUG -3.57%) is a choice between two distinct technologies. EOSE & PLUG: Performance Comparison Key Financial Metrics Eos Energy Enterprises specializes in zinc-based long-duration battery systems designed for utility and industrial applications. Plug Power focuses on building an end-to-end green hydrogen ecosystem, from fuel production to powering heavy machinery. Both companies are scaling rapidly but face different financial hurdles as they attempt to reach long-term profitability in the clean energy market. The case for Eos Energy Enterprises Eos Energy Enterprises designs zinc-based battery systems and is carving out a niche within industrial stocks. In its latest annual report, the company noted that two customers accounted for nearly 52% and 19% of revenue. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, though it highlights the scale of its current utility-level partnerships. In FY 2025, revenue reached about $114.2 million, representing a roughly 632% increase over the previous year. The company reported a net loss of approximately $970 million for the period. This performance follows a net loss of nearly $686 million in fiscal 2024 as the company continues to invest heavily in its manufacturing capabilities. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately negative 1.0x, indicating total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations with short-term assets, is nearly 4.9x. Free cash flow, which is cash from operations minus capital expenditures, was roughly negative $265.0 million in FY 2025. The case for Plug Power Plug Power builds an integrated green hydrogen ecosystem, deploying over 74,000 fuel cell systems globally. In its latest annual report, the company disclosed that Walmart Inc. (WMT +1.55%) was its largest customer, representing approximately a quarter of revenue. Such high customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the enterprise as it navigates the high costs of hydrogen infrastructure. In FY 2025, revenue reached about $709.9 million, which is a roughly 13% increase from the prior year. The company recorded a net loss of approximately $1.6 billion for the same period. This trend follows a net loss of roughly $2.1 billion in fiscal 2024, showing a slight narrowing of losses even as the top line remains volatile. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 1.0x, meaning total debt is roughly equal to shareholder equity. The current ratio is close to 2.3x. Free cash flow was approximately negative $662 million during FY 2025, reflecting the massive capital intensity required to build and operate hydrogen production facilities. Risk profile comparison Eos Energy Enterprises faces significant legal challenges from securities fraud class action lawsuits filed in 2026. These suits allege the company made misleading disclosures about its production ramp-up and quality issues at its Turtle Creek facility. The business also contends with competition from larger energy storage providers like Fluence Energy (FLNC -4.84%) and remains sensitive to changes in government subsidies. Plug Power is currently defending against multiple federal securities fraud lawsuits regarding its financial performance and Department of Energy loan status. The company suspended activities related to that loan program in November 2025, creating uncertainty about its path to low-cost capital. It also faces intense competition from established giants like GE Vernova (GEV -0.79%) while managing a complex supply chain for materials like iridium. Valuation comparison Eos Energy Enterprises is cheaper based on Forward P/E and earnings estimates, whereas Plug Power has a lower P/S ratio using sales over the past twelve months. Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers. Which stock would I buy in 2026? The current fiscal year, 2026, looks to be a major step forward for Eos Energy Enterprises. The business has already sold more products through the first half of the year than it did in all of 2025, shipping $126 million of gear to clients. The longer term should be much greater, too. Management says it has nearly $25 billion of business pipeline, meaning proposed energy storage developments Eos could bid on, and an $807 million backlog, which are firm orders for the company's products. 2026 revenue is expected to more than double. Recently, Eos scored a high-profile deal to support the PJM grid after joining with Alphabet Inc (GOOG +0.32%) and MN8 Energy on a solar energy storage project in West Virginia. Similarly, Plug Power's fuel cells run on clean-burning hydrogen, though creating hydrogen is often done in a process fueled by natural gas. Still, Plug Power sits firmly in the renewable energy niche, benefiting from many countries' moves toward green (non-fossil-fuel-derived) hydrogen. It is also benefiting from the datacenter boom and from restored tax credits that make its systems more affordable to deploy. For fiscal 2026, revenue growth is pretty good, with Wall Street analyst consensus predicting a nearly 15% increase to $812 million. The net loss is seen narrowing to about $580 million. Both businesses offer investors a way to play the rise in demand for power storage brought about by AI data center demand and the need for storage for renewable energy production. Eos, with its lower forward P/E and similar P/S ratio, seems to be the better bet for long-term investors.

artigo.texto: Why Choose TOPCon 3.0 Solar Modules? Vertex N G3 is built on Trinasolar's TOPCon 3.0 cell technology and incorporates four core technological upgrades. Ultra cell platform technology increases power output and bifacial performance. Multi-cut technology and edge passivation technology reduce current losses and improve shading and hot-spot performance. Ultra-high density packaging technology improves module efficiency and energy yield. A bifaciality of 85% ± 5% supports additional rear-side generation where site conditions allow, while the −0.26%/°C power temperature coefficient helps limit power losses in Vietnam's hot climate. A maximum annual degradation of 0.35% from the second year onward, backed by a 30-year power warranty, provides developers with a defined basis for modelling long-term output and project revenue. Solar and Battery Storage Applications in Vietnam Trina Storage also presented Elementa 3, its 6.25MWh utility-scale BESS built on in-house 587Ah cells. Elementa 3 supports renewable energy integration and flexible power supply, including in grid-connected projects, as Vietnam expands solar generation to meet growing demand from industry and AIDCs. Trinasolar's solar-plus-storage project at Corona Resort in Phú Quốc provides a local proof point of its PV and BESS delivery capabilities. The project combines a 3MWp solar installation with a 10MWh AC-coupled BESS retrofit, demonstrating how battery storage can be added to an existing commercial solar system. Vertex N G3 and Elementa 3 extend Trina's portfolio with higher module output and greater storage capacity per container, giving developers and EPC contractors greater flexibility in meeting project capacity and site requirements.

artigo.texto: Michael Burry adds BYD shares after calling automaker a potential low-cost leader Michael Burry, the investor known for predicting the 2008 housing-market crash, added shares of Chinese electric-vehicle maker BYD Company BYDDY BYDDF in a portfolio reshuffle disclosed in early October. The purchase was reported in an October 6 portfolio update on Burry’s Substack. The update also included changes to his positions in JD.com JD and several other stocks. The number of BYD BYDDF shares purchased and the size of the position were not disclosed. Burry’s earlier analysis outlined the investment case for BYD BYDDF, highlighting its valuation, manufacturing scale and technology. He wrote, “I would be an aggressive buyer at HK$75 or better, if the thesis still holds at that time.” He also highlighted BYD’s BYDDF cost advantages from controlling more of its supply chain. “BYD is potentially the lowest-cost producer of vehicles in the world thanks to its vertically integrated model at scale,” he wrote. Battery technology is another part of the investment thesis. BYD’s in-house Blade battery uses lithium iron phosphate chemistry. Burry’s analysis highlighted the chemistry’s cost and safety advantages over nickel-manganese-cobalt batteries, while acknowledging its lower energy density. He also pointed to international expansion as a potential source of operating leverage. “I believe BYD is an exceptionally well-run and technologically advanced company today, and I believe long-term ROIC will settle above 10%,” Burry wrote. In his March analysis, Burry also compared BYD BYDDF with Tesla TSLA, noting that BYD generated more revenue despite having a much smaller market capitalization. The comparison underscored his view that investors valued the two businesses differently. Burry had indicated in September that he was monitoring BYD BYDDF. artigo.texto: GLENDALE, AZ — The Phoenix area is experiencing a data center construction boom, transforming vacant lots and former farmland to meet digital demand in Arizona and beyond. Data centers keep the digital world running around the clock — streaming TV, cloud storage, banking, and artificial intelligence - but these facilities also require substantial power and water, which impact surrounding communities. DataCenterMap.com tracks locations worldwide and ranks Arizona eighth in the U.S. with 160 existing and proposed facilities statewide. Why is Arizona such a draw? "Land is inexpensive in Arizona; they require a lot of land to build," said Vijay Vittal, a professor at ASU's School of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering. Vittal said Arizona has also offered tax incentives and a geographic advantage "very close to the western tech markets" like California's Silicon Valley. Matt Bullock, Peoria's Mayor Pro Tem and owner of a data protection and cybersecurity company that works with data centers, echoed that assessment. "Arizona has one of the lowest seismic activity areas, unlike California or other parts of the country," Bullock said. "And because we have such wide open areas, it's very easy to get power and water infrastructure to data center locations." Data centers' demand for power and water — and the impact on nearby communities — is drawing pushback from some Arizona residents. April Butler lives near a proposed data center in Glendale called Project Eagle, also known as Project Baccara, located on Olive Avenue just east of the Loop 303. She says the project is massive. "The biggest part will be three data centers, and they're just back to back to back," Butler said. Butler and her neighbors spoke out at a Glendale City meeting in September. "I don't think we have a lot of laws in place to protect us," Butler said. "There are other states that were quicker enacting moratoriums and putting rules and guidelines in place to where it's a little bit more difficult to get those projects in." ABC15 is committed to finding the answers you need and holding those accountable. Submit your news tip to Investigators@abc15.com Peoria is also facing pushback over a large data center preparing to build there. Bullock said councilmembers are considering changes to zoning rules that would require special use permits for future data center projects or greater oversight. "To ensure they're using the reclaimed water, closed-loop [cooling systems], bring their own power, building parks and roads and things, and helping local schools," Bullock said. "That's how it should have been done all along, and now we're just catching up." As for Butler, she is standing her ground against Project Eagle. "Do you have any hope you can stop this from coming?" I asked her. "Absolutely," Butler said. A final vote on the formal land annexation and rezoning applications is expected at the Glendale City Council Meeting scheduled for October 27.

artigo.texto: INDEPENDENCE, Mo. — KSHB 41 reporter Tod Palmer covers sports business and eastern Jackson County, including Independence. Share your story idea with Tod. — Independence approved new zoning requirements for data centers and battery energy storage systems within city limits. After several months of conversation and public hearings, the Independence City Council unanimously approved the changes Oct. 5 to its Unified Development Ordinance, or UDO, related to such projects. Independence initiated a moratorium on new data center projects, which passed in July, over the summer after Nebius broke ground in May 2026 on a hyperscale AI data factory in the Little Blue Valley and Patmos moved to build a data center farther south along Little Blue Parkway. The council approved the Nebius project in March despite strong organized opposition, which ultimately led to residents voting out several council members who supported the project. Council member Brice Stewart and Mayor Kevin King introduced a series of amendments, all of which were also adopted unanimously. One requires any new data center or BESS developments to be at least 1,000 feet from residences or other public spaces — schools, parks, recreation and playground facilities, daycares, nursing homes, hospitals or places of worship. It would allow for variances, if recommended by the city planning commission and approved by the city council. Other amendments were related to noise-impact assessments and mitigation plans, decommissioning data centers that cease operations for 12 months, and requiring generator compliance reports every six months rather than annually. The new regulations require any data center larger than 2.5 megawatts to seek a special use permit from the city. Independence, like many city and county governments, didn’t have specific zoning requirements in place for data centers and BESS projects, which “present unique land use considerations not commonly associated with traditional industrial development,” according to the Agenda Item Cover Letter. Those complicated issues include massive electrical demand, high water consumption, on-site backup power generation, consistent mechanical noise and other issues. “The City's current UDO does not contain use-specific regulations for data processing and hosting facilities,” according to the cover letter. “As interest in this development type continues to increase, staff believes additional standards are appropriate to provide clear expectations for future development while protecting surrounding properties and community resources.” —

artigo.texto: BYD Chases Global Crown Without America as Battery and Storage Bets Deepen Published on 10/12/2026 at 13:40 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD has set its sights on becoming the world's largest automaker within five years, and it intends to get there without selling a single passenger car in the United States. The Chinese group is betting on purely organic growth, steering clear of the American market for now because regulatory hurdles facing connected vehicle software of Chinese origin make entry difficult. That global ambition is only partly reflected in the share price. The stock slipped 1.9% in the latest session to EUR 8.48, extending its year-to-date decline to 21%. A day earlier, the picture had looked brighter: BYD shares closed at EUR 8.65 on Friday, up 4.2%, lifted not only by company-specific news but by a broad recovery across Chinese automakers. According to media reports, the sector's rebound was a technical countermovement after several sessions of declines, with concerns about demand in the seasonal peak quarter and trade tensions between China and the European Union already partly priced in. Closing the Gap on Toyota and Volkswagen To narrow the distance to the industry leaders, BYD is pressing ahead with production capacity outside China. Toyota sold roughly 11.32 million vehicles worldwide in full-year 2025, Volkswagen around 8.98 million, while BYD delivered about 4.60 million. In the first half of 2026, Toyota notched 5.39 million sales, against 1.81 million for BYD in the same period. Management sees local supply chains as the key to closing that gap. Beyond plants already producing in Thailand and Uzbekistan, factories in Brazil and Indonesia are under construction. In Europe, the ramp-up at the Hungarian site is imminent, with series production slated to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026 once testing is complete. At the Paris Motor Show, Stella Li also held out the prospect of examining further European production locations in the medium term, with France among the candidates on the shortlist. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Public Fleets, Trucks and a Masdar Storage Deal Alongside its consumer passenger car business, BYD is broadening its international footprint in the public sector and adjacent technology fields. Overseas sales of passenger cars and pickups climbed 67.9% to almost 790,000 units in the first half of 2026. The company now supplies police forces and government fleets in several countries, including Mexico, Pakistan, the Philippines, Austria and Hungary. The commercial vehicle segment is expanding too. At its Huai'an plant, the 150,000th commercial vehicle in company history rolled off the line on October 9 — an all-electric Q3 tractor unit, underscoring the push into heavy long-haul transport. Outside vehicle manufacturing, BYD secured a battery storage agreement for 11.275 gigawatt-hours with energy company Masdar in the United Arab Emirates during the third quarter of 2026. Blade Battery Capacity Takes Precedence Operationally, BYD reports sustained strong demand for its models equipped with fast-charging capability. To safeguard delivery capacity over the long term, the company is giving top priority to expanding production capacity for the second generation of its in-house Blade battery. At the same time, the manufacturer is widening its model range at home. Pre-orders for the second generation of the Seagull have reportedly opened, with the official market launch planned for the fourth quarter. No official pricing has been disclosed so far. Geopolitics Keep Washington Off the Map On the international stage, management is pursuing a selective expansion strategy. Executive Vice President Stella Li, cited by Reuters, described geopolitical tensions as the single biggest challenge for the company's overseas business. For that reason, BYD will not bring passenger cars to the United States for the time being. Exports to other regions remain unaffected. In September 2026, the group sold 463,561 vehicles in total, a gain of 17.0% versus the same month a year earlier. Passenger car and pickup exports accounted for 180,700 units, up 153.9% from the prior-year figure. Ad BYD Stock: New Analysis - 12 October Fresh BYD information released. artigo.texto: UND in the Conversation: Data centers make heat all year long – here’s how the ground can hold onto it until winter Moones Alamooti, Assistant Professor of Energy and Petroleum Engineering at the University of North Dakota, explains in The Conversation how data centers generate waste heat year-round, and by storing that heat underground during warmer months, communities could reuse it in winter for heating buildings, reducing energy waste and reliance on fossil fuels. Editor’s note: The following article is written by Moones Alamooti and is an excerpt of the original article published by The Conversation. You can read the full article in its original format on their website. You have probably noticed it on a hot summer day: A basement feels cool even when the air outside is baking. The ground does not heat up and cool down as fast as the air does. A few hundred feet down, it stays close to the local yearly average all year, which can be around 50 degrees Fahrenheit (10 Celsius). In Verona, Wisconsin, the health software company Epic Systems has spent two decades turning that fact into infrastructure. It has drilled roughly 6,100 wells, 300 to 800 feet (90 to 240 meters) deep, that now heat and cool about 40 buildings on its own campus by using the waste heat from a 3.5-megawatt data center. What makes this setup unusual is not that Epic pulls heat out of the ground in winter – ordinary ground-source heat pumps do that in homes across the country. What’s uncommon is that Epic puts heat into the ground in summer and takes it back out months later. That matters more than it sounds because timing is what usually kills the idea of reusing a data center’s heat. Servers make heat every hour of the year. In most of the U.S., buildings need to be heated for only about four months. Piping it straight to nearby buildings works beautifully in February, but solves nothing in July. Storage is the missing piece.

artigo.texto: DE SOTO, Kan. — KSHB 41 reporter Isabella Ledonne reports on stories in Overland Park, Johnson County and topics about government accountability. Share your story idea with Isabella. — The company behind one of the hyperscale data center proposal projects in De Soto, Kansas, announced it is preparing to provide direct credits of up to $1,000 for every household in the city. Digital Realty is preparing its 300-acre site for a data center at Astra Enterprise Park near the Panasonic Plant. Construction is expected to start in 2027. Beale Infrastructure has started construction on its data center campus down the road from Panasonic and Digital Realty's site. But even with the promise of Digital Realty's money, neighbors are still skeptical of what the project could mean for their everyday life. "Is that enough?" neighbor Sara VanDeCreek said. "How much is the value of our community?" Digital Realty reached out to me on Friday to announce the company is planning to give every household a yearly credit up to $1,000 for the next 10 years to be used for property tax and/or utility relief. —Watch: De Soto data center plans to offer $1,000 to households; neighbors skeptical— It's among the first in the Kansas City metro to offer an incentive directly to residents. "De Soto has a lot of people that could use $1,000 a year," VanDeCreek said. But to some neighbors, that check could mean something else. "It's a bribe, is what it looks like," neighbor Toni Caldwell said. "If you can't give us the true answers, then don't come to me with money and expect me to believe what's going on or accept that money." Both Caldwell and VanDeCreek have been outspoken against De Soto's two data center developments, even helping launch a petition earlier this month to block the development. They explained that petition has gained more than 400 signatures. Digital Realty's announcement to invest $20 million in a community fund in the form of direct relief for residents has been met with some skepticism. "They're not really answering the questions that we have," VanDeCreek said. "I don't think it sweetens the deal and I think it's purposeful that it's coming out right now before they ask for tax incentives to help with bonds." I asked Digital Realty why the company is offering this and if it's meant to offset any anticipated rise in residential electric and water bills with the operation of the data center. "This commitment is designed to deliver tangible benefits for De Soto residents while we invest for the long term," a spokesperson said over email. "It accelerates benefits the community will receive and is a reflection of our broader approach to responsible development, collaboration and being a good neighbor in our project communities." "A community partner first of all is transparent," VanDeCreek said. Neighbors are still wanting answers to their biggest concern: the long-term impacts of having data centers in the community. It's a question residents say they haven't gotten the answer to with either data center proposal. "A good community partner is one you can trust," Caldwell said. "I don't trust either one of them right now." Digital Realty did not make anyone available for an on-camera interview. "This community investment accompanies Digital Realty's entire development in De Soto and reflects our long-term commitment to local partnerships," a spokesperson wrote in a statement. "We look forward to continuing this investment in the community as the project moves forward." The company is expected to have a TIF district public hearing at the city council meeting on Nov. 19. artigo.texto: Chinese electric vehicles are often cheaper because manufacturers combine affordable batteries, integrated production, large supplier networks and intense domestic competition. These advantages reinforce one another, helping automakers reduce costs across the vehicle rather than relying on a single saving. The International Energy Agency’s manufacturing comparison found that battery-electric vehicle production costs were more than 30 percent lower in China than in advanced economies. Batteries accounted for around one-third of the difference, while a similar manufacturing gap existed for conventional cars. The comparison used standardized small SUVs and 2024 cost data; it is not a universal discount across all Chinese models. The IEA’s 2026 research shows how this industrial advantage translates into affordable vehicles, while examples from BYD and overseas markets demonstrate why prices vary by location. Battery Prices Give Chinese EV Manufacturers a Head Start BloombergNEF’s 2025 battery price survey recorded a global average lithium-ion battery pack price of $108 per kilowatt-hour, down 8 percent from 2024. China’s regional average was $84/kWh. North American and European pack prices were respectively 44 percent and 56 percent higher. These regional averages cover multiple applications and battery chemistries, rather than identical automotive packs. An illustrative 60-kWh pack shows the financial effect: This calculation demonstrates the sensitivity of vehicle costs to battery prices. It is not a quotation for a particular EV battery. Manufacturers can use lower battery expenditure to reduce selling prices, improve margins or add features without increasing the final price. LFP Batteries Lower Material Costs Lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, batteries avoid nickel and cobalt in their cathode chemistry, reducing exposure to these expensive materials. The IEA’s Global EV Outlook 2026 battery analysis says LFP accounted for more than 55 percent of EV battery deployment in 2025, up from nearly 50 percent in 2024. China also produced more than 80 percent of global battery output. LFP is particularly useful for affordable vehicles where manufacturers balance purchase price, range and battery size. Higher-energy-density chemistries remain relevant for other applications, so the cheapest chemistry is not automatically the best choice for every model. Battery sizing creates another saving. At an illustrative $100/kWh, reducing capacity from 60 kWh to 45 kWh lowers pack expenditure by $1,500. The trade-off is less stored energy, making vehicle efficiency and intended use important. BYD Combines Battery Expertise With Integrated Vehicle Technology BYD provides a practical example of integrating battery and vehicle development. The company highlights its Blade Battery, Cell-to-Body integration and 8-in-1 electric powertrain as important technologies across its electric lineup. BYD reported selling more than 4.6 million new-energy vehicles in 2025, including battery-electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids. Integrated development can help engineers coordinate battery packaging, electronics and drivetrain design. Producing key technologies internally can also reduce some purchasing layers and simplify component coordination. However, vertical integration requires capital and manufacturing expertise. It supports lower costs when internal production is efficient and volumes justify the investment. BYD’s example therefore combines two advantages: control over important technologies and a large vehicle business over which to spread development expenditure. Factory Scale Reduces Costs When Capacity Is Used China produced approximately 16 million electric cars in 2025, exceeding domestic demand by around 20 percent, according to the IEA. Electric-car exports doubled to more than 2.5 million. These figures include battery-electric cars and plug-in hybrids. Large production volumes can spread tooling, engineering and factory overhead across more vehicles. For example, assume a plant has $200 million in annual fixed costs. Producing 500,000 vehicles allocates $400 per vehicle; producing 250,000 allocates $800. This simplified illustration excludes variable costs but shows why utilisation matters. High capacity alone does not guarantee low costs. Underused factories can increase unit costs, while manufacturers may cut prices to maintain output and clear inventory. Supplier Concentration and Automation Improve Efficiency China’s advantage extends upstream into battery materials. In 2025, it accounted for approximately 85 percent of cathode active-material production and more than 90 percent of anode active-material production used in electric-car batteries. Concentrated supplier networks can shorten delivery routes, support engineering collaboration and enable larger component orders. The IEA’s EV manufacturing cost analysis also identifies manufacturing efficiency and automation as major contributors to battery cost competitiveness. Shared vehicle platforms provide another opportunity. Using common motors, electronics and battery systems across several models can reduce duplicated development and tooling. As an illustration, $600 million in platform development expenditure spread across one million vehicles equals $600 per vehicle, compared with $1,200 across 500,000. Price Competition Makes Chinese EVs More Affordable The IEA’s 2026 electric-car market analysis found that average battery-electric car prices in China fell more than 10 percent in 2025. Around 30 percent of BEV models had entry prices below $20,000. Nearly 70 percent of BEVs sold in China were cheaper than their conventional equivalents before government incentives, indicating that affordability extends beyond consumer subsidies. Competition encourages manufacturers to pass savings to buyers. Nevertheless, selling prices and manufacturing costs are different measures: discounts may also reflect thinner margins or inventory clearance. Thailand Shows
