artigo.texto: Projects related to energy transition, green infrastructure development, green transportation, waste treatment, circular economy , and emission reduction activities often require large capital investments and long payback periods, while potentially involving technological and policy risks. Therefore, the challenge is not just how much capital is needed, but also where that capital comes from, with what terms and costs, and how the risks are distributed. Bank credit remains crucial, but it cannot alone meet the long-term capital needs. Along with credit, it is necessary to expand capital markets, green finance, climate finance, private capital, and risk-sharing mechanisms. But opening new channels of capital only solves half the problem. The harder part is determining what value a green project creates, where the risks lie, and to what extent that value can be converted into cash flow. This is where the carbon market becomes crucial. Carbon pricing creates an economic signal: emissions have a cost, while emission reductions can create value. For businesses, this signal can shift the balance between continuing to use high-emission technologies and investing in energy, fuel, or raw material-saving technologies. For projects that meet the credit mechanism, the resulting emission reductions can even become a source of revenue. However, carbon value only truly matters to investment decisions when businesses and investors have reason to believe that this value is clear, stable, and can be converted into monetary value. The gap between “potential emission reduction” and a tradable asset is therefore vast. Potential does not equate to tangible value. The creation of carbon value requires methodology, baseline data, and a measurement-reporting-verification (MRV) system, along with mechanisms for issuance, trading, and payment. Without one link, environmental value is not sufficiently solid to become a financial asset. Singapore's experience shows that a carbon market cannot be created solely through an exchange. The country combines price signals via carbon taxes with credit quality standards, international cooperation, and a financial services ecosystem. Policies create demand, standards build trust, and the financial system connects carbon value with capital flows. The lesson for Vietnam, therefore, is not just about building a place to buy and sell carbon credits, but about creating the necessary infrastructure for a market to form a reliable value. In Vietnam, this gap is evident in data and valuation, as emissions data remains fragmented, lacking sufficiently long data series and reliable benchmarks. Banks and investors struggle to reach a consensus on forecasting cash flows and pricing risks. Furthermore, the costs of due diligence, verification, and disclosure can also become a barrier for businesses. And especially, when information is not standardized, the "green label" alone is insufficient to build financial confidence. This also explains why green credit and carbon markets must be viewed within the same value chain. Capital needs arise very early, right from the project preparation stage, equipment procurement, technology investment, and production organization. Meanwhile, carbon revenue typically only emerges after emission reduction results are measured, verified, credits are issued, or sales contracts are formed. This gap creates a financial void that credit, bridge financing, guarantees, cash flow management, and combined financial mechanisms can fill. From a banking perspective, the appropriate approach is not to treat carbon credits as a guaranteed source of repayment from the outset. It's necessary to distinguish between cash flow from core business operations and carbon revenue. Core cash flow forms the foundation for repayment; carbon revenue is an additional layer and should only be recognized to the extent of certainty. Carbon value can impact the financial plan through three channels: reducing production costs through low-emission investments; reducing the need to purchase additional quotas for compliant businesses; or generating revenue from transferring emission reduction results or carbon credits. These three channels need to be quantified separately to avoid double counting or overestimating the potential for generating cash. On the capital market side, the requirements are similar. Carbon prices can only be passed on to the cost of capital when investors have sufficient information to assess risk. This requires verifiable data, consistent verification standards, clear disclosure, and post-audit mechanisms. When a project's emissions, emission reduction results, rights to carbon value, and projected cash flows are clearly defined, banks can better assess creditworthiness, and investors have a basis for valuing the asset. Therefore, unlocking green capital is not just about "getting more capital," but about creating a chain of links from emission reduction to data, from data to carbon value, and then to credit and capital markets. When this chain is transparent and reliable, the carbon market truly becomes a financial tool for green transition, instead of just a place to buy and sell credits. The ultimate measure lies not in the number of green labels or the scale of transactions, but in the actual emissions reduced, the number of projects funded, and the ability for the cost of capital to accurately reflect the quality, risk, and value of each project. The workshop focused on discussing the linkages between credit policy, carbon markets, and capital markets, thereby seeking solutions to unlock financial resources for the green transition process. artigo.texto: Rapid City to hold open house on proposed data center rules RAPID CITY, S.D. (KOTA) - Rapid City residents will have a chance to weigh in on proposed rules for data centers during a public open house on Oct. 14. The city’s Community Development Department will host the event Wednesday from 5 to 7:30 p.m. at City Hall in the Council Chambers and Circle of Friends Community Room. City staff will explain the proposed ordinance and collect public feedback. The proposal would expand rules adopted in December 2024, which defined data centers and allowed them in light and heavy industrial districts. New standards would address issues including setbacks from residential areas, power, water and sewer use, noise and vibration. The Planning Commission reviewed the proposal Sept. 10 but postponed further discussion until its Nov. 5 meeting to allow more time for revisions and public input. artigo.texto: (The Center Square) – The buildings that house thousands of computer servers powering cloud computing and artificial intelligence have increasingly caught heat over environmental and energy concerns. Another common criticism is that state and local governments offer data centers sweetheart deals to attract them, including tax breaks and other incentives, potentially leaving ordinary residents to shoulder some of the costs associated with their development. But the National Taxpayers Union has released a pair of studies in a series arguing that at least two common state tax policies treat data centers less favorably than other industries. Most states allow a tangible personal property tax on data centers, a tax the group contends is not only antiquated and generally harmful but disproportionately disadvantages data centers. The NTU also calls the tax an “international anomaly,” noting that “only seven of the 38 Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development countries tax tangible personal property at all, and among them, only Japan imposes them as broadly as the U.S.” A tangible personal property tax is a tax exacted on property “that can be moved or touched, such as business equipment, machinery, inventory and furniture,” as defined by the Tax Foundation. It’s paid annually and, like real estate property taxes, is calculated based on the assessed value of the property. For example, in some states, residents pay an annual property tax on their vehicles, often referred to as a car tax, based on the vehicle’s assessed value and the applicable tax rate. Data centers can pay tangible personal property taxes on their servers, networking equipment and other computer hardware, depending on state and local tax laws. Only, like with the car tax, the assessed value can be inaccurate. “Suppose the government thinks, ‘Well, your car is only two years old. It’s this make and model. You pay this much tax.’ But then you say, ‘Well, wait a minute! I drive this thing into the ground, and I’ve had to replace part of the suspension on it. It’s not in as good of shape as you think,’” NTU President Pete Sepp told The Center Square. Similarly, the assessed value of technology used in data centers can differ drastically from its market value — to the point that NTU argues state tangible personal property tax laws actually “discriminate against technology.” “The complex depreciation schedules required to value property are designed around manufacturing machinery that often performs at the same level after a decade or more of use,” NTU writes. “Applying the same standards to companies like data centers can significantly overvalue equipment like computer servers, which are often obsolete after three years.” And those depreciation schedules can also vary widely by state. In Florida, a three-year-old server is valued at 56% of its original cost according to its TPP tax law, while a handful of states would value that same server at 40% of its original cost. To avoid “discriminating” against technology-heavy industries like data centers, NTU recommends that states refrain from introducing new tangible personal property taxes but also avoid replacing existing ones with higher taxes elsewhere. And Sepp recommends going a step further. “State lawmakers should reform personal property laws so they’re uniform, neutral, simple and stable,” Sepp said in a statement. “Data centers are the manufacturing plants of the information age, and our laws should reflect that reality with equal treatment.” NTU also examined sales-and-use-tax exemptions in the first report of its series, addressing a more widely debated tax policy that has recently drawn criticism for its application to data centers. Thirty-three states offer a conditional form of the exemption to data centers (two offer it by right), but between May and August, eight states took steps to suspend or eliminate the exemptions “or benefit programs” for data centers, according to an analysis by S&P Global Market Intelligence. In the two states that offer sales-and-use-tax exemptions to data centers without having to meet special investment or employment requirements, the exemptions allow data centers to purchase computer servers, networking equipment and other hardware without paying applicable state and local sales taxes. Such exemptions are often perceived as unique to the industry, but that is a misconception, according to NTU Senior Fellow Jared Walczak, and “betrays a misunderstanding of how sales taxes are supposed to work.” There is a general consensus in tax policy that sales taxes should apply to final consumption rather than the inputs used to produce goods and services so as to avoid tax pyramiding, which occurs when a good or service is taxed multiple times at different stages of the production and supply chain, inflating the final consumer price. For example, if a data center pays sales tax on its computer servers, it may pass that expense along to businesses that use its computing services. Those businesses may then pass the added cost along to their customers through higher prices, which are taxed again when consumers make purchases. “No state’s perfect on exempting business inputs, but there are a few bright lines that basically all states adhere to,” Walczak told The Center Square. “They don't tax raw materials, and they almost always exempt machinery and equipment.” The vast majority of states offer sales tax exemptions for machinery and equipment used in manufacturing, while exemptions are also available for equipment used in industries such as agriculture, mining and energy production. “The problem is, where do data centers fit in that? Are they manufacturing? You know, what are they?” Walczak said. “A lot of states didn’t have a ready-made category for that.” Many states created similar exemptions years ago for data centers through incentive programs to help attract data centers, but unlike in manufacturing, in 33 states, data centers’ equipment

artigo.texto: The zoning amendment, filed by Mayor Dominick Pangallo in July, defines data centers within the city’s zoning ordinance, as a “facility, or portion thereof, primarily designed or used to house computer servers and related information technology infrastructure for the storage, processing, management, or transmission of electronic data.” City staff and legal counsel determined that data centers were already not an allowed use under the current zoning, but there was no language until now to explicitly define a data centers and prohibit its construction in the city. All councilors favored moving some version of the zoning amendment forward. Most of the discussion Thursday night centered around what version of the amendment would prevent potential loopholes for developers to exploit without inadvertently banning routine data processing uses for businesses such as hospitals and telecommunications. During a committee meeting Sept. 30, Councilor at-Large Ty Hapworth made a revision to specify that “a data center shall not include such computer servers and related information technology infrastructure that is accessory, incidental, and subordinate to a lawful principal use at the same facility or a portion thereof, however stored. This exception does not cover a separate business providing data storage, server hosting, distributing processing, or similar technology to third parties.” Several councilors agreed they need to revisit the new zoning change in the coming months, saying that what the mayor initially filed left them with little flexibility to more carefully define data centers without banning routine data processing. Legally, the council is unable to substantially change the language beyond the “four corners” of what was originally proposed in July. Since the council plans to revisit the matter soon, councilors Lydia King and Jason Sydoriak said it would be best to exclude Hapworth’s amendment in order to prevent potential loopholes. “We can all agree that nothing we can pass tonight is a comprehensive data center ordinance,” King said. “There is a lot of nuance that would go into (that), so anything we do tonight is effectively temporary... (But) by further clarifying accessory uses, we may have inadvertently introduced additional loopholes that would make this harder to hold up against in court if someone wanted to come and say they didn’t like a ruling they got from the city.” Other councilors disagreed. “I think this language is valuable to keep in here,” said Ward 6 Councilor Katelyn Holappa. “If this use is ‘accessory, incidental, and subordinate to a lawful principal use’ — all of those three things together, such as a hospital having a server room, we’re not making that impossible. That could cause problems for businesses that we’re not intending to put in here.” The vote to include Hapworth’s proposed language passed, with just King and Sydoriak in opposition. The committee had also approved a motion to strike language previously recommended by the Planning Board adding the language “and has an aggregate power demand of 2 Megawatts or higher” to the end of the definition of data centers. Councilors shared concerns that a use of up to 1.9 megawatts could still result in harmful impacts associated with data centers such as heat and noise. Ultimately, the council unanimously approved the zoning change to ban data centers, with plans to revisit the issue in the coming months to draft language that would give a more comprehensive definition of data centers. © 2026 The Salem News (Beverly, Mass.). artigo.texto: The Chinese battery manufacturer leads with 26,574 patent families, supported by substantial research investment and rapid advances in power and solid-state battery technologies. China’s Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Limited (CATL) has surpassed South Korea’s LG Energy Solution to become the world’s leading company in battery patent holdings, highlighting China’s growing influence in the global battery technology sector. According to data released on October 6 by intellectual property consulting firm PatSnap, CATL recorded 26,574 simple patent families between October 2016 and September 2026. This places it ahead of LG Energy Solution, which holds 22,597 patent families, creating a gap of nearly 4,000. Simple patent families group patent applications covering the same core invention across different countries or regions. This method provides a clearer comparison of companies’ technological contributions while avoiding duplicate counting of identical inventions. CATL Strengthens Its Position in Battery Innovation The latest rankings reflect a significant shift in the battery industry, where Japanese and South Korean manufacturers historically held leading positions in research and development. LG Energy Solution now ranks second, while Panasonic has dropped out of the top ten with 4,994 patents. Toyota remains the only Japanese company among the leading ten. CATL’s growing patent portfolio is backed by substantial research spending. The company has invested more than 100 billion yuan, equivalent to approximately $14.9 billion, in cumulative research and development. PatSnap data further indicates that CATL holds 27,402 battery patents overall, including 16,722 filed during the past three years. These recent filings account for 61% of its total portfolio, demonstrating the pace of its technological expansion. Power Battery Patents Lead the Industry CATL has established a particularly strong position in power battery technology, holding 19,539 patents. Its portfolio is approximately 2.2 times larger than that of the second-ranked domestic competitor. During the past three years, CATL filed 12,084 power battery patents, significantly exceeding the 4,384 recorded by its closest domestic rival. Its recent filings also approach the combined 14,500 patents held by companies ranked second through fifth. Solid-State Battery Research Gains Momentum CATL is also expanding its presence in solid-state battery development, a technology widely viewed as important for the next generation of energy storage. The company holds 3,538 patents in this field, more than twice the total of its second-ranked domestic competitor. Of these, 2,763 were filed during the last three years, nearly matching the combined 2,891 patents recorded by domestic companies ranked second through tenth. The figures underline CATL’s growing technological lead and the increasingly prominent role of Chinese manufacturers in shaping the future of battery innovation.

artigo.texto: Morocco prepares to launch Africa’s first battery gigafactory Gotion Power Morocco plans to begin equipment commissioning in Kenitra, advancing major investment in battery manufacturing KENITRA, Morocco (MNTV) — Morocco is preparing to advance its electric vehicle battery manufacturing industry as Gotion Power Morocco plans to begin commissioning production equipment at its Kenitra gigafactory during the week of October 20. Moroccan subsidiary of China’s Gotion High-Tech announced the timetable for starting up equipment at the industrial facility, which is intended to produce lithium iron phosphate battery cells. The project’s first phase represents an investment of approximately 13 billion Moroccan dirhams, equivalent to about $1.3 billion, and targets an initial annual capacity of 20 gigawatt-hours. Located in Kenitra’s Atlantic Free Zone, the facility is designed to serve the automotive and energy storage industries. Its potential markets include Morocco, other African countries, Europe, the Middle East and the United States. Construction began in September 2025, with the company’s buildings and infrastructure completed over approximately 13 months. The project required large-scale shipments of production equipment from China, supported by Moroccan port and customs authorities. Gotion Power Morocco president Khalid Qalam described the equipment startup as an initial step toward developing a wider battery manufacturing ecosystem in the country. The company has recruited more than 400 Moroccan employees, including engineers, technicians and production workers. Many received training at Gotion facilities in China before joining the Kenitra project. The company expects the gigafactory to create more than 2,300 direct jobs when fully developed. Its longer-term plans include expanding production capacity and manufacturing battery materials for electric vehicles and energy storage systems. The project also forms part of a broader partnership involving Gotion and Volkswagen’s battery subsidiary, PowerCo. The companies announced a separate Moroccan joint venture in September to produce lithium iron phosphate cathode materials. That venture is expected to involve an investment of approximately €480 million, or about $547 million, with planned annual production capacity of 100,000 metric tons. The developments strengthen Morocco’s ambitions to attract advanced manufacturing investment and establish a larger role in international electric vehicle supply chains.

artigo.texto: Four-Hour Battery Storage Now Cheaper Than Gas Turbines: Report Lower battery costs, gas turbine shortages, and fuel volatility aid storage October 12, 2026 Follow Mercom India on WhatsApp for exclusive updates on clean energy news and insights Four-hour battery energy storage systems, utility-scale energy storage systems that are designed to discharge at their full rated capacity for approximately four hours, now cost less than open-cycle gas turbines across 43 markets, according to Wood Mackenzie’s latest global report on levelized cost of electricity (LCOE). This shift is driven by technological advancements and evolving market dynamics. Single-axis tracking solar is the lowest-cost new power generation option in 43 of the 48 markets analyzed. Wood Mackenzie attributed the shift to declining battery costs, gas turbine shortages, and volatile fuel prices. North America U.S. solar costs face pressure from tariffs, antidumping and countervailing duties, and Section 232 import restrictions. Utility-scale solar is partly insulated by 168 GW of safe-harbored capacity, although module prices are projected to rise 5% annually through 2030. Residential and commercial solar projects face greater cost pressures, with module prices expected to increase 6% in 2027 and 14% in 2028. Onshore wind’s LCOE is projected to decline 16% by 2060, driven by lower capital and operating costs, despite policy uncertainty and potential tariff impacts. Tax credits are expected to support battery storage economics despite foreign entity of concern restrictions and supply chain constraints. Storage costs could rise after investment tax credits phase out in 2038. Technological advances and domestic manufacturing expansion are projected to reduce storage LCOE by 10% by 2060. Growing data center demand is likely to constrain gas generation equipment supply through the late 2030s, keeping capital costs elevated. Latin America Single-axis tracking solar so far remains Latin America’s lowest-cost power generation technology in 2026. Its average costs are projected to decline 38% by 2060. Brazil, Chile, and Mexico benefit from strong solar resources and high capacity factors. Onshore wind’s average LCOE is projected to fall nearly 21%, from $73/MWh to $58/MWh by 2030, supported by the expansion of Chinese manufacturers and larger turbines. Grid-scale battery storage is expanding through renewable energy-linked mandates and standalone procurement. Its LCOE is projected to decline 42% by 2060. Offshore wind costs are expected to approach parity with combined-cycle gas turbines, before firming, in the early 2040s. Asia Pacific Utility-scale solar remains the most cost-competitive power source in Asia Pacific, although costs differ substantially across markets. In 2026, solar generation costs in the region’s most expensive market are over 200% higher than in the cheapest. The gap is expected to widen to 250% by 2030, despite declining costs across all markets. Onshore wind costs vary more than sixfold across the region. Greater penetration of Chinese turbine manufacturers and the adoption of higher-capacity turbines are expected to narrow the cost gap with coal in South and Southeast Asia. China has the world’s lowest grid-scale storage costs, more than 55% lower than the rest of Asia Pacific’s average of $134/MWh. Chinese equipment supply is expected to reduce the regional average to $92/MWh by 2036. Japan, Australia, and the Philippines face higher costs due to import duties, installation expenses, and domestic manufacturing policies. Offshore wind costs outside China are expected to decline significantly from the early 2030s. Europe Solar remains Europe’s cheapest power generation technology. The LCOE for fixed-tilt systems is projected to decline 22% by 2060, despite a 14% increase in capital expenditure (CAPEX) in 2026 due to higher module prices. Onshore wind CAPEX is expected to decline 2.5% annually through 2030 as manufacturers benefit from improved financial stability and growing demand. Higher capacity factors are expected to bring its LCOE to $60/MWh by 2060. Battery storage turnkey CAPEX rose 2%, the first increase in three years, as cell prices rebounded 10% from 2025 lows amid stronger demand and higher lithium prices. CAPEX is projected to decline 12% by 2031, although rising lithium prices could slow subsequent reductions. Europe has the highest fossil fuel generation costs among the regions analyzed, with carbon costs expected to exceed fuel costs by 2030. Offshore wind costs are projected to decline from the 2030s as supply chains stabilize and turbine prices fall. Middle East and Africa The Middle East and Africa have the lowest regional LCOE for single-axis tracking solar, at $37/MWh in 2026. Costs are projected to decline to $24/MWh by 2035, while solar LCOE in Saudi Arabia and the UAE could fall below $20/MWh by 2033. Onshore wind costs are declining as Chinese turbines become more competitive. Egypt and Morocco have low wind generation costs, supported by capacity factors of 40% to 45%. Four-hour battery storage costs in the region are estimated at $120/MWh in 2026 and are projected to decline 33% to $80/MWh by 2035. Battery storage is more cost-competitive than open-cycle gas turbines across the region’s gas markets, supporting the integration of solar and wind and reducing reliance on gas-fired peaking capacity. According to Wood Mackenzie, renewable energy LCOE across major markets, including single-axis tracking solar in the Middle East and Africa, recorded the lowest regional LCOE of $37/MWh as of November 2025, driven by technological advances, supply chain stabilization, and improved module efficiencies. Battery storage project costs hit an all-time low in 2025, even as other renewables rose, according to BloombergNEF’s LCOE 2026 report.

artigo.texto: A PNAST fechou a primeira Temporada de Acesso em 7 de outubro com 367 pedidos e mais de 20 GW na fila. A conta de quem paga, o que muda para quem quer conectar uma usina e as datas do próximo ciclo. A PNAST deu o primeiro resultado prático nesta semana. O Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) fez na terça-feira (6) o primeiro processo competitivo da política. Entregou 228 MW da rede básica de transmissão a três data centers em São Paulo, segundo o balanço divulgado pelo ONS e pelo Ministério de Minas e Energia. Sete projetos disputaram, somando 451 MW de demanda habilitada. Quase metade do que foi pedido ficou sem conexão na rede básica: 223 MW. O Decreto nº 12.772, de 5 de dezembro de 2025, é o texto que criou a PNAST e define as regras. O que é a PNAST, em português claro? Até o decreto, quem queria ligar uma usina ou uma fábrica grande à rede entrava numa fila por ordem de chegada. Agora o acesso permanente acontece em Temporadas de Acesso, janelas em que todos os interessados registram o pedido e o ONS analisa tudo junto. - Energia renovável perde ritmo no Brasil com cortes de geração e incerteza para investidores - Áustria teve 43.300 tickets em 10 minutos para disputar R$ 215 milhões de subsídio solar que paga R$ 838 por kWp, enquanto no Brasil painel novo já paga 60% do Fio B - Usina solar de Indiana instalou 20 mil painéis por dia com 1.800 operários em 18 meses e está prestes a operar - Agricultor de Illinois tem 10 torres eólicas na fazenda e recebe cerca de R$ 600 mil por ano, mas no Nordeste os relatos vão de R$ 600 a R$ 2 mil por mês por torre Onde o pedido total passa do que a rede básica aguenta, a vaga vai a leilão. O decreto manda fazer “processos competitivos dos pontos de conexão onde a demanda registrada superar a capacidade disponível”. A política vale para geradores e consumidores que queiram usar a rede básica, conforme a página da PNAST no ONS. Ficam de fora as distribuidoras de energia. Quanto custou a vaga e quem ganha com isso? Os lances médios ficaram na ordem de R$ 800 por kW. A informação é da associação das transmissoras, a Abrate, em nota divulgada ao Canal Solar. A conta, feita aqui: 228 MW são 228 mil kW. Multiplicados por R$ 800, dão cerca de R$ 182 milhões. É uma estimativa, porque o valor é uma média aproximada e o ONS não informou, nas fontes que li, o total arrecadado. O caminho do dinheiro está no decreto. As receitas dos processos competitivos “serão revertidas para a modicidade tarifária”, ou seja, para segurar a tarifa de energia. A regra detalhada fica com a Aneel, a agência reguladora. Quanto isso pesa na conta de luz de casa, nenhuma fonte calculou. Quem levou a capacidade? Duas das vencedoras, a Pahlavan One e a Pahlavan Three, são ligadas à norte-americana CloudHQ, que desenvolve um campus em Paulínia (SP), de acordo com a Eixos. A terceira é a Digital DC Brasil, que opera com a marca NextStream. A disputa foi só em São Paulo, em quatro pontos de conexão da rede básica. Nenhuma das usinas solares e eólicas do país aparece entre os vencedores desse primeiro leilão, pelas fontes que li. Os data centers levaram tudo. Onde entram as usinas solares e eólicas? As usinas solares e eólicas estão na mesma fila de pedidos da Temporada de Acesso. A temporada registrou 367 empreendimentos de geração e consumo, somando mais de 20 GW em solicitações, espalhados por 64 barramentos do Sistema Interligado Nacional. Somando a fase de transição, o ONS analisou mais de 43 GW. Desses, cerca de 30,7 GW foram viabilizados ou habilitados. As fontes não separam quanto desse total é solar, eólica ou carga, e essa divisão ficou sem resposta. A Abrate liga a política à expansão das usinas solares e eólicas e da geração distribuída. Liga também à chegada de grandes cargas, como data centers e hidrogênio verde. É a mesma rede para todos, e a Temporada de Acesso é o novo caminho para as usinas solares e eólicas e para os data centers. O que muda para quem quer conectar uma usina? Pelo decreto, três mudanças pesam para o dono de uma usina, solar ou eólica: - O pedido deixa de valer por data de chegada. O interessado precisa entrar na janela da Temporada de Acesso, com dados do projeto. - Onde há mais pedido que vaga, o ponto de conexão vira disputa, com lance. - O ONS passa a abrir duas temporadas por ano a partir de 2027, segundo o decreto, e avisa o cronograma com 90 dias de antecedência. Resta uma dúvida que o decreto não resolve sozinho: o preço da vaga. A nota técnica de metodologia só sai em 4 de dezembro, segundo o calendário publicado pelo ONS. A regra do lance depende dela. Quando abre a próxima Temporada de Acesso? O ONS publicou em 7 de outubro o calendário da primeira Temporada de Acesso de 2027, de acordo com o Times Brasil. O próprio ONS avisa que as datas ainda podem mudar. A novidade para quem já ganhou leilão de energia é a rota própria. Esses projetos são habilitados um mês antes da conta da vaga na rede básica. Nada garante, porém, que a capacidade seja suficiente em cada ponto. O que o gerador deve fazer agora? O cadastro abre em janeiro, mas o trabalho vem antes. Para a Temporada de Acesso de 2027, estudos, dados técnicos e a estratégia de uso da rede precisam estar prontos antes de 4 de janeiro, observa o Times Brasil. O diretor-geral do ONS, Marcio Rea, afirmou na cerimônia de encerramento que o primeiro ciclo mostrou a efetividade do novo modelo. A avaliação é do próprio operador. Quem pode medir é o investidor, quando a regra do lance sair.

artigo.texto: AI introduces unprecedented challenges in data centers; not just in power, but in cooling, latency, deployment speed and geography. These challenges carry through all data center areas, or “subsystems,” to varying degrees. These different subsystems often require tailored solutions in an AI data center, removing them from any semblance of a typical “uniform” design. Setting a foundation for a successful AI implementation requires a cable infrastructure partner with the capacity, agility and resources to deliver high-performance cabling systems designed for real-world data center environments. It also requires an understanding of how AI implementation interacts with each subsystem in the data center, and what the people responsible for maintaining those subsystems can expect. There are four key subsystems: the Entry Point, Front End, DC Interconnect and Back End Subsystems. Entry point The Entry-Point subsystem is traditionally part of the data center gray space, supporting infrastructure by connecting the cable coming from outside the data hall to the cable within it. Moreover, the entry point is where those fibers are separated and directed to different areas of the facility. Increasing density demands from AI applications are driving increases of high fiber count cables coming into the Entry Point, and increasing power and cooling demands have further limited available gray space in the data center. This can cause complications for space utilization, cable management and labor, resulting in speed of deployment being the most critical issue related to the entry point. So how can data center operators mitigate this issue? Rapid and versatile installation is key; innovative splicing enclosures, splicing and interconnect trays and consideration of pre-terminated solutions can be vital. These solutions unlock a modular approach to infrastructure, allowing for rapid and easy upgrades as needs evolve and require much less time to install overall. Front end The Front-End subsystem is typically in the white space, where the computing occurs inside the data center, and is the layer that handles traffic between users, internal resources and external networks. Of the four subsystems, the Front End is least impacted by the addition of AI, buoyed above the waves that hit other subsystems by its established infrastructure. The Front-End Subsystem’s foundation has only received minor updates over the last five years. However, local code compliance is almost always a concern when expansions occur on the frontend, especially when those expansions are in other geographic locations. Global solutions can alleviate this concern, allowing you to utilize the same infrastructure across locations where local codes differ slightly. Data center interconnect The DC Interconnect subsystem is part of the data center’s gray space, or areas that provide critical support for computing, and often consists of multiple high strand count fiber cables running between facilities that connect pods across the network. Somewhat ironically, AI struggles with the capability that the DC Interconnect subsystem was designed to deliver: connection over distance. An AI cluster on the back end is treated as a single system, housed in one location that then must spread itself over the rest of the facility. As the size of AI clusters increases, expansion of the data center interconnect system also grows exponentially to ensure that communication between facilities at maximum throughput. However, the data center interconnect system is notoriously difficult to expand, demanding time and labor to add or replace cabling. Leaders can mitigate this issue by deploying infrastructure that can handle the higher densities AI requires, while also being built for rapid deployment. Leviton’s 1728-strand MMC trunks, which are part of the STRATA™ family of Hyperscale and AI data center solutions, allow for a much higher density footprint than traditional alternatives. Moreover, Leviton’s trunks are designed to be installed quickly and easily – a huge boon when recabling a traditionally labor-intensive subsystem. Back end Finally, there’s the Back End; the subsystem that houses the AI cluster, and where AI implementation really changes the subsystem’s status quo. As the density of the system increases to accommodate the AI cluster, cable management and power become critical. The substantial power demands of AI technologies require data center operators to find ways to do more with their established power infrastructure. The challenge of managing the increased density is one that data center operators are familiar with; doing more with less. This is where Very-Small-Form-Factor (VSFF) connectors, like MMC, come in. VSFF connectors meet the need for higher density at connect points, while taking up less space than their MPO alternatives. This enables operators to scale fiber capacity without proportionally increasing rack space, as demonstrated by solutions such as Leviton's STRATA™ family, which supports up to 3,456 fibers per rack unit using a 16-fiber MMC connector. As for maximizing the potential of established power infrastructure, utilizing power more efficiently in the data center often boils down to cooling. Immersion cooling is an emergent technology wherein servers are submersed in non-electrically conductive, thermally conductive fluids, offering almost-instantaneous heat dispersion for high-density networks. The success of immersion cooling depends not only on thermal performance but also on ensuring network infrastructure can operate reliably in submerged environments. Solutions such as Leviton TORRENT™ are designed to address this challenge by maintaining signal integrity and resisting degradation in dielectric cooling fluids. artigo.texto: Fox stays positive on data centers even as public backlash grows The News Despite increasingly critical media coverage of AI and the spread of data centers across the US, one news network has been painting a more positive picture. More than half of the references to data centers on Fox News over the last two years would have left viewers with a favorable impression, compared to less than 10% on CNN and 5% on MS NOW, according to a new Semafor analysis of mentions of data centers on each network. The mentions were pulled from closed captions preserved by the Internet Archive, which keeps a digital, searchable library of recorded TV news. A pair of AI models from Anthropic and OpenAI scored each reference on its content, with the network's name removed. Mentions of data centers have, predictably, shot up across all three networks in recent months as political backlash against AI swells and the data centers themselves have become a salient issue ahead of the midterms. But Fox's opinion and morning shows, including, , and leaned on the promise of AI, economic investment and the race with China, skewing Fox's coverage more favorably, the analysis showed. The network's news shows were more measured. In an Aug. 23 monologue that at one point featured a chyron reading "The case for data centers," Fox host Brian Kilmeade acknowledged "real concerns," but argued that "saying no to data centers nationwide also means saying no to the tax dollars that can flow into a community. … If Americans don't build the infrastructure to meet the demand, somebody else will." On CNN and MS NOW, the criticism focused as much on the facilities' political toxicity as on harms like power bills or water use, casting them as unpopular with voters and a liability for politicians who back them heading into the midterms. Data centers "are driving up energy costs, sucking up water supplies, wiping out rather than creating jobs," MS NOW's Katy Tur said in May. "Politicians beware." Polling shows that across demographic groups, Americans hold increasingly negative views of data centers: More than half of Americans say data centers are mostly bad for the environment, Pew Research Center found last month, compared with 39% in January. Fox News did not comment for this story. Max's view The pro-data center programming on Fox News comes as the right tries to define its positions in an AI-fueled, post-Donald Trump future. Fox's favorable data center coverage mirrors Trump's position on their growth and the need for AI companies to help fuel the US economy. "The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor," Trump wrote on Truth Social in August. "If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame." But anger about data centers and the rapid advancement of AI represents a faultline within the MAGA coalition that swept Trump back into office. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis and Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., have questioned some data centers in their states, while Texas Gov. Greg Abbott seems to have flipped from supporting data centers to looking to slow their growth in his state amid a tougher-than-expected reelection campaign. Some on the right I have talked to in the last several months worry that Fox News, which Trump watches religiously, and other pro-data center voices are encouraging the president to take positions that are broadly unpopular with his rural and suburban base. "The Big Tech oligarchs, the guys driving AI, did a terrible job," Steve Bannon, a staunchly anti-AI Trump ally, told the Daily Signal in September. "They came in to try to muscle local communities, and particularly since President Trump's strongest base is in exurban and rural communities, that's where they were really the ugliest, and they haven't made their case, and they particularly haven't made their case at the local level about the economics of this, and the energy of this, and the water of this, and the manifestation of what these things are going to be used for." Room for Disagreement Not all of Fox's data center coverage has been rosy; its tenor grew slightly less favorable in 2026 compared to last year. "It's taxing our system way too much on water, agriculture land, or electricity. We're gonna implode," the Texas agriculture commissioner said in an interview on a weekend Fox show in August. "We just can't do it. There's not enough.

artigo.texto: Bulgaria’s net electricity exports surged by 62% in annual terms from the beginning of the year to early October. They reached 3.5 TWh, compared to 2.16 TWh in the same period last year, driven primarily by increased generation from renewable energy sources, supported by energy storage systems. Data from Bulgaria’s transmission system operator (TSO) Electricity System Operator (ESO) show that the country produced 12.24% more electricity year-on-year, while domestic consumption grew by 8.45%, according to the Association for Production, Storage and Trading of Electricity (APSTE). Power generation from renewable energy sources reached 11.5 TWh, up by nearly 34% from the previous year. Renewables have accounted for nearly 80% of the country’s total power generation growth. The expansion of energy storage systems has been particularly remarkable The expansion of energy storage systems has been particularly remarkable. From the start of the year until October 4, grid-scale batteries delivered 1,720 GWh of electricity to the power system. It is a more than ninefold increase from just 190 GWh that was recorded a year earlier. This enabled cheap electricity generated during the day to be stored and used during hours of higher demand and higher prices, APSTE pointed out. Of note, Bulgaria’s BESS capacity is approaching 6 GW / 17 GWh. Eurelectric earlier said that 5.4 GW of BESS capacity accounts for 22.8% of total generation capacity in the country, making it one of the global leaders. Bulgaria remained a net exporter during the challenging summer in the region APSTE stressed that the benefits of the new energy mix became particularly clear during the summer. Despite prolonged heatwaves and low water levels on the Danube river that constrained nuclear and hydro power generation across the region, Bulgaria remained a net exporter and maintained prices lower than neighboring markets during key periods. This success was driven by a combination of solar power plants, battery storage, and the Kozloduy Nuclear Power Plant (NPP). Gazdov: While neighboring markets suffer from high prices and power shortages, Bulgaria generates and stores more and more of its own electricity “While neighboring markets suffer from high prices and power shortages, due to constraints on their nuclear plants and high natural gas prices, Bulgaria generates and stores more and more of its own electricity. This translates into more competitive prices for households and businesses, greater energy security, and a stronger position on the regional energy market,” APSTE chairman Nikola Gazdov explained. A striking example occurred on October 8, when Unit 6 of the Kozloduy NPP underwent planned maintenance and Unit 5 operated at reduced capacity due to low water levels on the Danube. Despite these constraints, in the early afternoon photovoltaic systems were producing nearly 4,300 MW, exceeding total national demand of 4,100 MW, while batteries were charging at over 4,000 MW, storing cheap electricity for peak evening demand, the update reads. Wind is the solution for cheaper electricity in the winter However, APSTE warned that the successful expansion of solar energy and batteries is not enough. In the winter, solar generation decreases while demand rises. To secure more of cheap domestic power during the colder months, Bulgaria must accelerate wind energy deployment. Since 2020, PV capacity in the country has grown by about 600% to nearly 7 GW, while BESS capacity is close to 6 GW / 17 GWh. APSTE estimates that total investments in photovoltaics, batteries, and related infrastructure since 2020 have reached approximately EUR 7 billion. However, Bulgaria has only 716 MW of installed wind capacity, with no major new wind farm built since 2013. Wind power complements solar with a different daily and seasonal generation profile, capable of providing substantial power output during winter, APSTE added. Gazdov: Sun and batteries have significantly enhanced Bulgaria’s energy security “Sun and batteries have significantly enhanced Bulgaria’s energy security amid one of the most severe energy crises. This is very important, but it is not enough. We must build on this success by attracting investment into wind power as well,” he said. This road will secure cheaper local electricity not only in the summer, but also in the winter, Gazdov added. Achieving this does not require new subsidies, but clear rules and a genuine easing of construction procedures for new capacity, in his view. According to APSTE, Bulgaria could attract over EUR 4 billion in additional private investment in wind farms and energy storage systems by 2030, provided institutions ensure predictable regulations and remove unnecessary administrative constraints, including for projects located outside renewable energy acceleration areas.

artigo.texto: Residents weigh in on year-long data center pause CHARLOTTE, N.C. – Dozens of people sounding off about whether Charlotte should move forward with data centers in the city. City council hosted a public hearing to extend the data center moratorium. Across the country, conversations about data centers have been getting heated but the discussion at the government center Monday night was subdued. More than 30 residents on both sides of the argument signed up to speak at the hearing. Back in June, the council voted in favor of a data center moratorium that runs out in November. The moratorium temporarily paused any new data center applications or development. This did not stop projects that are already under construction like the large scale data center under construction in University City. The moratorium was supposed to give staff time to research potential ways to regulate data centers and address environmental concerns. The city started a task force and hosted forums for residents to weigh in while working on regulations. More than 100 days later the work isn’t done. “Staff need additional expertise and capacity to develop the tools needed to ensure responsible data center development,” Heather Bolick, Chief Sustainability & Resiliency Officer for City of Charlotte said. “An extension of the moratorium would allow us to develop needed tools.” Some residents encouraged the city to speed up the process of writing regulations for data centers. “We believe that this moratorium is an impractical tool that risks sending the wrong signal about our region’s economic readiness,” Rob Nanfelt, Executive Director of Real Estate and Building Industry Coalition said. “However, since city staff and council require more time to study infrastructure impacts, we firmly believe the path forward lies in collaboration, not exclusion.” Other residents say the city cannot afford to rush the process to regulate data centers. “The purpose of a moratorium is not to stop progress; is to create the space for informed progress,” Rev Dr Janet Garner Mullins, Charlotte resident said. “Tonight is not about whether data centers belong in Charlotte. It’s about whether or not Charlotte has done enough homework before writing rules that would shape our future.” Some councilmembers suggested city staff research what other cities are doing to regulate data centers. Council will vote on whether to extend the moratorium at the October 22nd meeting. If passed the action would extend the moratorium until October of 2027.

artigo.texto: The flagship seven-seater is BYD’s first vehicle in Europe to feature its second-generation batteries and Flash Charging tech, delivering over 400 miles of range. BYD launches new flagship Atto 8 in Europe “BYD is all about turning intelligence into reality,” Stella Li, the company’s executive vice president, said on Monday. The Atto 8 is the “perfect example,” Li added, featuring its latest breakthrough tech, including its second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging system. Introduced at the Paris Auto Show, the flagship SUV is the first BYD vehicle to feature its Flash Charging system, enabling it to recharge just as fast as filling up at the gas station. It takes just five minutes to charge from 10% to 80%. A full recharge, or going from 10% to 97%, takes just nine minutes. According to BYD, that’s about a third of the time rival SUVs take to go from 10% to 80%. Even in temperatures as low as -30°C, it requires only 12 minutes for the vehicle’s battery to recharge from 20% to 97%. Measuring 5,040 mm long, 1,996 mm wide, and 1,760 mm tall, the Atto 8 is about the size of other full-size electric SUVs, such as the Hyundai IONIQ 9 and Kia EV9. BYD’s flagship SUV comes in two all-electric variants with the choice of rear- and all-wheel-drive powertrains. The Design RWD model has a single rear motor producing 456 hp (340 kW) and 269 lb-ft (365 Nm) of torque, which BYD said delivers a 0 to 62 mph time of eight seconds. Powered by a 115 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery, the Atto 8 offers an impressive WLTP range of up to 405 miles (600+ km). For example, BYD said the flagship SUV offers enough electric range to drive from London to Edinburgh. The Atto 8 Excellence AWD, on the other hand, adds a front electric motor for a combined output of 764 hp (570 kW) and 572 lb-ft (775 Nm) of torque. The added power delivers a sports-car-rivaling 0- 62 mph acceleration time of 4.6 seconds and a WLTP range of 374 miles. Inside, natural light fills the spacious cabin thanks to a 2.39m2 panoramic glass roof. Both Atto 8 variants have a 10.25″ digital instrument cluster, a 26″ head-up display, and a 15.6″ central infotainment touchscreen with Google Built-in. BYD said the Atto 8 is specifically tailored for those looking for a “zero compromise” seven-seat SUV. The front seats and outer seats of the middle row feature heating, ventilation, and massage functions. Rear passengers get their own air-conditioning control panel. All seats are upholstered in genuine leather. The Design RWD model features a 10-speaker sound system, while the Excellence AWD gains a 21-speaker DiSound audio system, plus an added front refrigerator. With the second and third rows folded, the Atto 8 offers up to 1,960L capacity. Even with all three rows up, the full-size SUV offers 270L of luggage space. Plus, there’s a 136L frunk (front trunk). BYD said dealers in Europe will begin selling the Atto 8 in the first quarter of 2027. Prices have yet to be announced, but given it will be positioned above the Ti 7, a plug-in hybrid seven-seat SUV, it will likely start at slightly over £47,995 ($65,000) on the road in the UK. In Europe, BYD currently sells the Tang, an electric seven-seat SUV. In Germany, the BYD Tang typically starts at €75,000 ($84,000), but it’s currently on sale for €47,990 ($54,000).

artigo.texto: Modelos e plataformas de IA Flex adiciona módulos de IA fabricados em fábrica ao portfólio de data centers modulares Adicione Unite.AI às suas fontes preferidas no Google Em 12 de outubro de 2026, a Flex anunciou um portfólio ampliado de soluções modulares pré-fabricadas para data centers, projetadas para acelerar a implantação de fábricas de IA de próxima geração. O portfólio inclui os novos Axiom AI Modules, que integram energia, computação de alta densidade e resfriamento líquido avançado em sistemas fabricados em fábrica, que, segundo a Flex, podem reduzir os prazos de implantação em até 50% em comparação com a construção tradicional. O portfólio ampliado faz parte do segmento de Infraestrutura de Nuvem e Energia da Flex, que a empresa planeja separar e transformar na Axiom Solutions International, Inc., uma empresa independente de capital aberto, no primeiro trimestre do ano-calendário de 2027. A Flex afirmou que, à medida que a infraestrutura de IA cresce em escala e densidade de potência, os operadores de data centers enfrentam complexidade cada vez maior na distribuição de energia, no resfriamento, na integração da computação e na implantação. Chris Butler, que deverá ocupar o cargo de diretor de tecnologia e estratégia da Axiom, afirmou que atender a essa demanda em escala exige mais do que melhorias incrementais. Em vez disso, descreveu uma abordagem em nível de sistema que combina tecnologias de energia, computação e resfriamento com manufatura avançada para simplificar a integração, acelerar a implantação e fornecer fábricas de IA em escala. Por dentro dos Axiom AI Modules Segundo o comunicado, os módulos integram componentes essenciais da infraestrutura de IA em três categorias. Um rack de energia de 800 VDC oferece conversão e distribuição de energia de alta eficiência para a infraestrutura de IA de 800 VDC de próxima geração e a computação de alta densidade. Unidades avançadas de distribuição de resfriamento fornecem resfriamento líquido para controlar o calor gerado por cargas de trabalho de IA que consomem muita energia, enquanto racks de TI de alta densidade integram servidores de IA, redes e interconexões de alta velocidade para dar suporte à computação de IA de próxima geração em escala. A Flex afirmou que transferir a integração de infraestruturas complexas do local do data center para um ambiente de fábrica controlado permite montar, integrar e testar os módulos em paralelo ao desenvolvimento do local, reduzindo a complexidade no local e ajudando os clientes a disponibilizar capacidade de IA mais rapidamente. Uma página de recursos da Flex publicada em 12 de outubro de 2026 informa que os módulos são pré-fabricados e comissionados em um ambiente de fábrica controlado, com racks de TI e a infraestrutura de suporte essencial integrados em um único sistema antes do envio. Os módulos incluem estruturas de corredores, unidades de distribuição de líquido refrigerante, redes secundárias de fluidos, painéis de energia remotos, controles, sistemas de distribuição elétrica, sistemas de gerenciamento da qualidade da água e componentes de segurança e detecção de vazamentos. Prazos de implantação estimados A página de recursos apresenta uma comparação estimada entre a implantação modular pré-fabricada e a construção tradicional com estrutura montada no local para um projeto de fábrica de IA, tomando como referência os 18 meses, ou 78 semanas, da construção tradicional. Nesse modelo, afirmou a Flex, os Axiom AI Modules podem reduzir os prazos de implantação em até 50%, de 78 semanas para apenas 39 semanas. A Flex atribuiu a aceleração a cinco fatores: padronização do projeto e integração em fábrica; fabricação em fábrica e construção no local em paralelo; redução da instalação, dos testes e do comissionamento no local; controles integrados e testes no nível dos racks; e menos alterações em etapas avançadas, retrabalho e falhas de instalação em campo. A empresa declarou que os prazos e as economias reais de implantação variam conforme o escopo do projeto, as condições do local, os requisitos de projeto e outros fatores. Presença industrial e separação da Axiom A Flex afirmou que está desenvolvendo ativamente soluções modulares pré-fabricadas para hiperescaladores em suas unidades em todo o mundo, com o apoio de mais de três milhões de pés quadrados de capacidade dedicada à fabricação de infraestrutura de data centers nos Estados Unidos. Em conexão com a separação proposta, Flex apresentou à Comissão de Valores Mobiliários dos Estados Unidos (SEC), em 5 de outubro de 2026, uma declaração de procuração no formulário Schedule 14A. A declaração de procuração foi enviada ou divulgada por outros meios aos acionistas para solicitar sua aprovação das propostas relacionadas à cisão. A declaração de registro da Axiom no formulário Form 10, referente às suas ações ordinárias, foi apresentada à SEC em 15 de setembro de 2026. Em um comunicado separado, de 5 de outubro de 2026, a Flex informou que havia firmado um acordo para vender US$ 2,0 bilhões em ações preferenciais conversíveis Série A da Axiom a fundos afiliados à General Catalyst e à Koch Equity Development, além de coinvestidores, com um valor empresarial inicial de US$ 37,5 bilhões para a Axiom. Revathi Advaithi, CEO da Flex e futura CEO da Axiom, afirmou que o investimento “fornece financiamento por meio de capital próprio para nossa aquisição da EPC Power, anunciada recentemente, e permitirá que a Axiom tenha um balanço sólido enquanto nos preparamos para nos estabelecer como uma empresa independente de capital aberto”. As ações preferenciais conversíveis pagam dividendos em dinheiro de 10,0% ao ano antes da separação. Depois dela, a taxa cai para 6,0% ao ano se pagos em dinheiro ou 7,0% ao ano se pagos na forma de dividendos não pecuniários, sujeita a aumentos após o quinto aniversário da separação e a certos outros ajustes. A General Catalyst terá o direito de indicar um diretor para o conselho da Axiom após a conclusão da separaç

artigo.texto: AI data centers got the "Weekend Update" treatment on "Saturday Night Live" this week. Comedian James Austin Johnson portrayed "Shark Tank" investor Kevin O'Leary on the sketch comedy show, during which he addressed the dispute over the real O'Leary's proposed data center in Utah, known as the Stratos Project. "It's very simple. All I want is to buy up 40,000 acres of God's untouched splendor and replace it with a very loud computer that steals your job," Johnson's O'Leary said. "Is it going to take up precious water? Absolutely. Is it going to provide a necessary service? Who's to say? But on the flip side, it's going to make me a tremendous amount of money, and I think that's great." The "SNL" version of O'Leary said he understood that some Americans were concerned about data centers near their homes. (An actual May Gallup poll found that over half of American surveyors opposed constructing AI data centers in their local area.) "These things are terrible and shouldn't be anywhere. That's why I'm building one in Utah," he said. Data centers are a contentious issue in the United States. Leading tech companies rely on AI data centers to power their systems and products. Supporters say they'll create new jobs, bolster the economy, and help the US defeat China in the race to control the global AI market. Residents in the places where they are being built, however, are often much less excited about them. The Utah project, backed by O'Leary Digital, has drawn criticism from many local residents over concerns that the data center could strain local resources and worsen the environment. Some residents are also upset over what they consider a lack of transparency from O'Leary and local leaders. Critics of the Stratos Project have staged protests, created petitions, and taken legal action to stop its construction. O'Leary scaled back the data center's size from about 40,000 to just over 20,000 acres after public pushback. He has said he remains undeterred, though. "There are bumps in the road. There's litigation. There's misinformation. There's propaganda. You name it. But if you know what you're doing is right, you make it, you get there," O'Leary told Business Insider in June. "Persevere." During a May interview on Fox News, O'Leary said said some critics of the project have ties to the Chinese Communist Party, a claim he later walked back. A Utah advocacy group that has publicly opposed the project filed a defamation lawsuit against Fox News and O'Leary in July. On "Saturday Night Live," Johnson's O'Leary acknowledged the incident. "I made the mildly inflammatory claim that every single person in Utah who opposes me is a paid communist super agent from China. Was I wrong? Perhaps. But just because they're not, doesn't mean they aren't," he said. He added, "I'm going to make the future go away. And we're doing just that in Utah."

artigo.texto: Battery Storage Beats Gas Peakers. Is Canada Backing the Wrong Horse? October 10, 2026 | Markham on Energy According to a new report from consulting giant Wood Mackenzie, battery storage is now cheaper than gas peaker plants in almost every market. Analysts are hailing the milestone as a seminal moment for the electrification of the global economy – or, as we like to call it, the energy transition. Granted, this is an important moment. But it’s also just one data point in a process of technological change that will end many decades in the future. And, in that change, there is a critical lesson for Canada at this point in our country’s economic evolution. I’ve been writing about technological change for four decades. My model is based on the transition from horses and steam to tractors and modern industrial farming from 1900 to 1950. In that process are all the components of most technology adoptions. The slow initial development of the technology (1900 to 1920, when the first modern “small tractors” appeared in the market). The adoption inflection point (1920, with the introduction of the Fordson, cheap and built on automotive manufacturing). The mid- to late-1920s, when ancillary machines (the combined harvester-thresher, the three-point hitch, rubber tires) became available. Then, from 1930 to 1950, the now-superior economics of mechanical agriculture displaced horses from every field in North America. The story over the past 75 years has been about ever-improving technology and changing farm economics. But the war between the technologies – animals and steam versus the internal combustion engine – was fought in the first half of the 20th century. Pegging the date for the start of the modern technology competition – combustion vs electrotech, molecules vs electrons – is inexact, but let’s choose 2010. Comparatively speaking, then, we’re 16 years into a 50-year transition. In 2060, we’ll look back on that process and the triumph of electric over combustion will appear inevitable. Just as the triumph of the tractor seems inevitable from today’s vantage. That’s why the Wood Mackenzie analysis is interesting, but not cause for popping the champagne. The triumph of battery storage is one data point among many in a long, complex process. A decade from now we might have enough data to declare electrons the victory, just not quite yet. But one thing we can say for certain: if present trends hold, electrons will win. And that any country that wants to have an advanced, prosperous economy in 2060 has to bet on the tractor, not the horse. This is the lesson for Canada. Four-Hour Batteries Are Beating Gas Peakers on Cost Gas peaker plants fire up when electricity demand surges, supplying power for those relatively short periods when the grid needs extra help. Batteries that can deliver electricity for four hours increasingly compete for that job. Wood Mackenzie now finds their lifetime cost per unit of electricity is lower than that of open-cycle gas turbines in all 43 markets where it compared the technologies. The competitive gap is widening: turbine shortages and volatile fuel prices push up gas costs, while expanding battery manufacturing pushes storage costs down. The significance extends beyond batteries taking business from gas plants. Storage makes solar and wind more useful by saving electricity for when customers need it. Cheaper batteries therefore expand the market for other electric technologies, just as better implements expanded what farmers could accomplish with a tractor. This is the technological convergence at the heart of our theory of change: advances in one technology create opportunities for others, strengthening the economics of the emerging system. The Same Competition, Different Regional Advantages China shows what manufacturing scale can accomplish: its grid-scale storage costs are more than 55 per cent below the average for the rest of Asia Pacific, according to Wood Mackenzie. In the Middle East and Africa, abundant sunshine makes the combination of solar and batteries especially attractive. Four-hour storage already undercuts gas peaking across the region’s modelled gas markets, and WoodMac forecasts its cost will fall another 33 per cent by 2035. Different regional advantages are pushing the competition in the same direction. Across the rest of Asia Pacific, China’s manufacturing strength is helping drive storage costs lower. Wood Mackenzie expects competitive Chinese supply to help bring the regional average, excluding China, down from US$134 per megawatt-hour to US$92 by 2036. Japan, Australia, and the Philippines are expected to remain more expensive because of import duties, installation costs, and domestic manufacturing policies. The broader significance is that China’s investment in scaling electric technologies is changing the economics of energy well beyond its borders. North America illustrates how messy that competition can become. Tax credits help battery storage compete, while trade restrictions and supply-chain constraints push in the opposite direction. Meanwhile, data-centre demand is straining gas-generation supply chains, keeping capital costs elevated and strengthening the investment case for renewables and storage, according to WoodMac. The technologies compete within markets shaped by government decisions, industrial capacity, and changing demand. The direction of technological change can be clear even while the path remains uneven. Another lesson for Canada: whether 4-hour batteries are more competitive than gas peakers in Canada is the wrong question. The right one is the effect on electrification promoted by falling battery storage costs in the Global South where Canada hopes to sell Alberta oil and British Columbia LNG. More EVs mean falling demand for gasoline and diesel. More heat pumps and grid-storage batteries mean less demand for gas. artigo.texto: Seres Group has signed a long-term strategic agreement with Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL) in Chongqing, securing CATL battery supply for every AITO model in its line-up. Concluded on 10 October 2026, the pact also enlarges their shared battery production and adds joint work on supercharging, battery services and overseas markets. AITO, the premium brand Seres develops with Huawei, has used CATL packs in every model since launch, with deliveries now past 1.2 million vehicles. Extending that arrangement across the full range gives Seres supply certainty and hands CATL a customer with proven volume. Production is the most concrete strand. The partners will fast-track phase two of their plant-in-plant facility inside the Seres Super Factory, adding 10 to 12 GW/h a year for a combined total above 20 GW/h. Building batteries inside the vehicle plant is meant to sharpen cost competitiveness, and the expansion also supports Chongqing’s drive to build a cluster of intelligent connected electric vehicle makers. Beyond the factory, the companies plan supercharging networks and battery services that follow a car through its whole life. They will also seek buyers together in the Middle East, Central Asia and Europe, a spread that gives AITO growth options outside the EU, where China-built electric cars face extra import duties. Source: CATL

artigo.texto: Priorizar a melhoria do quadro institucional e garantir o funcionamento eficaz da bolsa de carbono. Para garantir a implementação eficaz de tarefas essenciais relacionadas às mudanças climáticas, o Vice-Ministro da Agricultura e do Meio Ambiente, Le Trong Yen, solicitou ao Departamento de Mudanças Climáticas que priorize a conclusão do projeto de lei que altera e complementa diversos artigos da Lei de Proteção Ambiental, bem como os projetos de decretos e circulares que orientam sua implementação. Ao mesmo tempo, ele instou à aceleração da pesquisa e do desenvolvimento da Lei de Mudanças Climáticas. Com relação ao mercado de carbono, o Vice-Ministro orientou a implementação da Conclusão nº 71-KL/TW, de 17 de julho de 2026, do Comitê Central do Partido, sobre a gestão e o uso de créditos de carbono para servir ao desenvolvimento socioeconômico sustentável e garantir a segurança nacional, em um espírito de estreita ligação com a prática, criando uma fonte de bens e um mecanismo de negociação transparente para que a troca opere de forma eficaz, trazendo benefícios práticos para as pessoas e as empresas. Ele também orientou a aceleração da conclusão do banco de dados nacional sobre mudanças climáticas, conectando-o ao Centro Nacional de Dados do Ministério da Segurança Pública , para servir efetivamente à gestão, operação e exploração de recursos pela sociedade. Ao mesmo tempo, o Departamento está preparando meticulosamente cenários para a participação em negociações internacionais na próxima conferência COP 31, visando afirmar a posição do Vietnã e suas contribuições responsáveis no cenário internacional. Segundo o Diretor do Departamento de Mudanças Climáticas, Nguyen Tuan Quang, nos últimos três meses de 2026, o Departamento concentrará todos os recursos na conclusão do sistema de documentos legais imediatamente após a aprovação da proposta de emenda à Lei de Proteção Ambiental pela Assembleia Nacional; na implementação da Conclusão nº 71-KL/TW, de 17 de julho de 2026, sobre a gestão e o uso de créditos de carbono para servir ao desenvolvimento socioeconômico sustentável e garantir a segurança nacional, e da Conclusão nº 75-KL/TW, de 28 de julho de 2026, do 3º Plenário do 14º Comitê Central do Partido Comunista do Vietnã sobre proteção ambiental e resposta proativa às mudanças climáticas na nova era; na aceleração da reforma dos procedimentos administrativos e na continuidade da coordenação da operação da bolsa de carbono; na organização da reunião do Comitê Conjunto Vietnã-Japão em outubro; na preparação meticulosa da delegação internacional e na modernização da infraestrutura do Banco de Dados Nacional de Mudanças Climáticas. Você também pode gostar Olhando para o futuro, até 2030, a unidade definiu como foco continuar a aprimorar o quadro político, pesquisando proativamente e preparando uma proposta para a Lei de Mudanças Climáticas, com um plano para submetê-la à Assembleia Nacional em 2029. Nos primeiros nove meses de 2026, o Departamento prestou consultoria proativa e concluiu diversas tarefas essenciais, conforme diretrizes do Comitê Central, do Governo e da liderança do Ministério. Entre elas, o Departamento liderou o desenvolvimento do plano de gestão e utilização de créditos de carbono, que serviu de base para a publicação da Conclusão nº 71-KL/TW pela Secretaria. Simultaneamente, o Departamento colaborou com o Ministério do Meio Ambiente na elaboração da Conclusão nº 75-KL/TW, de 28 de julho de 2026, do Comitê Central do Partido Comunista do Vietnã, sobre proteção ambiental e adaptação proativa às mudanças climáticas na nova era; e concluiu e submeteu para publicação o Programa de Ação Governamental completo e o Programa de Ação do Ministério para a implementação dessa conclusão. O Departamento coordenou-se estreitamente com o Departamento do Meio Ambiente para finalizar o projeto de lei que altera e complementa diversos artigos da Lei de Proteção Ambiental, para que o Governo o apresente à Comissão Permanente da Assembleia Nacional. O projeto encontra-se atualmente em fase de revisão técnica para garantir sua apresentação em tempo hábil à Assembleia Nacional, para apreciação e aprovação na sessão de outubro. O progresso na elaboração de documentos políticos e legais, de acordo com o programa de trabalho de 2026, está dentro do cronograma, sem atrasos em nenhum documento. De agora até o final do ano, o Departamento continuará a desenvolver um Decreto e uma Circular em paralelo com o projeto de alteração e complementação de diversos artigos da Lei de Proteção Ambiental, visando garantir a coerência do sistema jurídico. O Departamento recomendou ao Ministério que submeta ao Governo uma Resolução aprovando o Acordo de Implementação do Artigo 6º do Acordo de Paris entre o Governo do Vietname e o Governo de Singapura. Atualmente, o Governo aprovou acordos bilaterais de troca de créditos de carbono com Singapura e o Japão; relativamente à Coreia do Sul e à Suíça , o Departamento está a promover negociações técnicas, prevendo-se a assinatura até ao final do ano. Você também pode gostar Em relação aos inventários de gases de efeito estufa, o Departamento mantém inventários em nível nacional, organiza sessões de treinamento para orientar empresas no cálculo e na redução de emissões e está estabelecendo um sistema online de relatórios de inventário para reduzir custos e melhorar a transparência dos dados. Além disso, o Departamento está finalizando um plano para preparar a participação da delegação vietnamita em importantes conferências internacionais sobre o clima ainda este ano.
