artigo.texto: - Meta built a massive AI data center cluster in Ohio - And it innovated several new infrastructure techniques for that data center - Now, the company is building the world's biggest data center in Louisiana OCP GLOBAL SUMMIT, SAN JOSE, CALIFORNIA — The Open Compute Project (OCP) conference has been around for about 15 years, but 2026 is definitely its biggest year, so far. About 15,000 people are attending the sold-out conference to get together and talk about compute hardware. And more specifically, to talk about compute hardware and infrastructure for AI. A speaker from Meta Platforms kicked off the conference this afternoon with his presentation about Meta’s AI data centers. And he kind of blew everyones’ minds. Santosh Janardhan, head of Global Infrastructure with Meta, first talked about solving multiple problems for the company’s huge data center complex in New Albany, Ohio, which is named Prometheus. And then he gave a preview of Meta’s new, gargantuan data center in Richland Parish, Louisiana. Prometheus includes over 30 structures, millions of miles of fiber-optic cables and tens of thousands of GPUs. “Constructing it ended up being quite an epic journey,” said Janardhan. One of the first problems Meta had to solve was the networking between all the different structures. Historically, data centers have been built as a single building, under one roof. But in the case of Prometheus with its multiple structures, the distances between the buildings would have caused unacceptable time delays for connectivity. “When you do AI training, it moves forward at the speed of the slowest conversation that you can have between two GPUs,” said Janardhan. “The physics is simple. You essentially want to create a lossless network.” To do this, Meta created what Janardhan called an “Ethernet super spine.” He said, “You take the spines of all the buildings in the region, string them together and aggregate them locally.” The advantage is that there are no stops, so no single points of failure. “And the other thing to understand here is that this thing is fast — tens of petabits a second,” he said. “You can transmit the whole Library of Congress in less than 30 seconds.” (For a deeper technical dive into Meta’s data center inter-building networking, check out this blog.) He also noted the massive amounts of fiber optic cable needed for Prometheus, showing the below photo of some of the cables. “Each one of those pipes that you see are serving actually thousands of strands of fiber,” he said. “In fact, if you aggregate all the network fiber we have in Prometheus, it's about three to four million kilometers of fiber. You can go to the moon and back, four times. The physical manifestations of AI training truly boggles your mind.” Another problem that Meta solved was speeding up the construction of buildings. Historically, data centers have been built with steel and concrete. But Meta re-thought that because it wanted to build its data centers faster. So, it decided to build tents, instead. “Each one of our tents is the length of minimum two football fields, he said. These are humongous. And this takes months to build, not years. Because time-to-market matters.” But he said the tents are “fairly robust” — rated for a category 1 hurricane — “because you’re putting in billions of dollars’ worth of equipment in it.” While it was reimagining everything about data centers, Meta figured — why not also reformulate concrete? Janardhan said, “I don't think people understand how much concrete is used in the world. And it’s not great for the environment. It takes a lot of energy and water to create concrete. And when cities are paved with too much concrete, it creates an unpleasant heat-island effect, which contributes to more global warming. "So what we did is we fundamentally went after the composition of concrete,” said Janardhan. “We built an AI tool to rethink how concrete works, and the new concrete that we ended up getting uses 19% less carbon, cures 43% faster, and is completely cost-neutral.” Meta is open sourcing its AI tool for the concrete formulation. “All of you can go and use it,” he said. “Use it in your data center. Use it in your backyard.” Hyperion will be even bigger Now, Meta is taking the lessons it’s learned from Prometheus and applying them to its next AI data center cluster — Hyperion, in Louisiana. “That’s going to be absolutely mammoth,” said Janardhan. It's a five-gigawatt cluster at a single location. To the best of my knowledge, it’s the biggest data center on the planet. It covers about 4,000 acres.” At this point in his speech, the audience was in awe with the magnitude of Meta’s innovation and the sheer scale of its projects. But then, Janardhan said, “What matters is what runs on this, right? At the end of the day, every call, every message, every interaction, every post you do on one of the properties, that has real meaning to someone, right?” And then the audience realized that this was all for properties such as Facebook and Instagram, and that blew the wind out of the sails for many of us. artigo.texto: Credo Launches Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Standardization for AI Data Center Scale-Up and Scale-Out Applications Joined by Initial Participants Including Leading Hyperscaler and Optical Technology Solution Providers AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics, SENKO, and YOFC Under the OCP Networking Project SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 12, 2026-- Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (Credo) (NASDAQ: CRDO), an innovator in providing connectivity at scale through fast, reliable, and energy-efficient system solutions, alongside prominent optical technology providers, today announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. Among the first to join with Credo include a leading hyperscaler as well as AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics,SENKO, and YOFC, bringing together expertise spanning the full optical connectivity stack to advance the development of the wide, parallel optical connectivity ecosystem. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261012753816/en/ Credo, alongside prominent optical technology providers, has announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. Micro-emitter technology brings new ways of moving volumes of data, while dramatically improving reliability, power efficiency, and bandwidth density. Arrays of micron-scale light sources make up the transmit side of an optical link. Rather than pushing a few optical channels to extreme data rates, many micro-emitters operate in parallel at optimal individual speeds, enabling layer zero redundancy to improve reliability. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. The specification, targeted for OCP approval in 2027, will address requirements for link power, efficiency, signaling, parallelism, physical form factors – including module and connector footprint, link budget, and compliance. By defining specifications, the SRMO Workstream aims to give data center operators, hyperscalers, and system designers access to a broad ecosystem of interoperable components with supply chain resiliency, accelerating time to deployment and fostering continued innovation in optical connectivity. “As AI workloads scale from thousands to tens of thousands of accelerators, the industry needs a standardized approach to wide, parallel optical connectivity — not a patchwork of components that do not fit together or interoperate,” said L.K. Bhupathi, Associate Vice President of Product at Credo. “Launching the SRMO Workstream reflects Credo’s commitment to solving the interconnect challenges facing AI infrastructure collaboratively, alongside those who will build, deploy, and depend on this ecosystem. We believe that defining specifications, developed through industry collaboration, is the fastest path to bringing wide, parallel optics to scale.” “We continue to advance our micro-emitter, micro-receiver and 3D packaging technologies enabling next-generation wide and parallel AI optical interconnects that support very high bandwidth density,” said Ashkan Seyedi, Vice President and General Manager of Digital Photonics Interconnect at ams OSRAM. “Joining the SRMO Workstream is an important part of our strategy to bring the benefits of reliability, efficiency, and simplicity to connectivity in the AI data center.” “Realizing the power and density benefits of a micro-emitter approach depends on getting the physical connector interface exactly right, especially as channel counts scale into the thousands,” said Obie Roy, Vice President of Strategic Commercial Development at SENKO Advanced Components, Inc. “The SRMO Workstream represents an important industry effort to establish a common connector interface that can bring a new level of density and reliability in next-generation data center architectures.” More information about the SRMO Workstream can be found here. About Credo Credo’s mission is to transform connectivity at scale through fast, reliable, and energy-efficient system solutions. Our high-speed copper and optical interconnect technologies deliver industry-leading power and performance from chip to cluster to meet the ever-expanding data infrastructure demands of AI. Our vertically integrated connectivity portfolio is comprised of our flagship purple ZeroFlap (ZF) Active Electrical Cables (AECs) and ZF optical transceivers; optical components including silicon photonics-based photonic integrated circuits (SiPho PICs) and DSPs; OmniConnect AI memory and chip-to-chip interconnect; and retimers for Ethernet and PCIe—supported by our PILOT diagnostic and analytics software platform. Credo innovations enable our customers to connect the systems that connect the world. For more information, please visit https://www.credosemi.com. Follow Credo on LinkedIn. artigo.texto: Credo Unveils 1.6T ZeroFlap Active Light Cable, Industry's First Row-Scale, Wide-Parallel Optical Interconnect for AI Data Centers Micro-Emitter-Based, Pluggable Solution Targets Scale-Out and Front-End Connectivity Up to 50m with Copper-Class Reliability at Lower Power and Reduced Cable Bulk SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 12, 2026-- Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (Credo) (NASDAQ: CRDO), an innovator in providing connectivity at scale through fast, reliable, and energy-efficient system solutions, today shared details of its 1.6T ZeroFlap active light cable (ALC), the industry’s first row-scale, wide-parallel optical interconnect solution built for AI scale-out and front-end networks. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261012663213/en/ Credo's ZeroFlap Active Light Cable (ALC) is based on a dense array of micro-emitters and photodetectors coupled with flexible, lightweight fiber bundles, designed to draw 12W per cable-end in a pluggable form factor. With targeted reach up to 50m alongside 100 million hours mean time between failures (MTBF), Credo’s ZeroFlap ALC is designed to deliver the reliability, power efficiency, and reach required for next-generation AI infrastructure. The ZeroFlap ALC is based on a dense array of micro-emitters and photodetectors coupled with flexible, lightweight fiber bundles, designed to draw 12W per cable-end in a pluggable form factor. With targeted reach up to 50m alongside 100 million hours mean time between failures (MTBF), Credo’s ZeroFlap ALC is designed to deliver the reliability, power efficiency, and reach required for next-generation AI infrastructure. The 1.6T ALC architecture will be featured in Credo’s booth at the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit this week in San Jose. News Highlights - Credo's ZeroFlap ALC will bring wide-parallel, micro-emitter optics to row-scale reach, closing the mid-reach gap between copper's distance limits and the power and cost overhead of traditional pluggable optics. - The cable splits 200G lanes into many low-rate optical channels using simple NRZ modulation, avoiding the power and latency costs of complex DSP-based signal processing. - Built-in channel redundancy and ZeroFlap link monitoring enable hitless failover, with target reliability of 100 million hours MTBF and bit error rates better than traditional optics. - The ZeroFlap ALC is designed to draw 12W per cable-end, roughly 30% less than comparable active electrical cables (AECs), is 10x lighter than AECs and extends the reach to 50m enabling row-scale connectivity. As AI clusters expand across data center rows, operators need connectivity that combines greater reach with reliable, energy-efficient operation. Credo’s 1.6T ZeroFlap ALC will extend the reliability principles behind its field-proven AEC solutions to a new optical architecture. Micro-emitter technology harnesses optical arrays that make up the transmit side of a link. Rather than pushing a few optical channels to extreme data rates, many micro-emitters operate in parallel at optimal individual speeds. This shift from “fast-and-narrow” to “slow-and-wide” enables lower power per bit along with optical links protected with redundancy. “For decades, optical transceivers have prioritized data rate per fiber. Our 1.6T ZeroFlap ALCs are engineered with reliability as the first-order concern,” said L.K. Bhupathi, Associate Vice President of Product at Credo. “The scale-up and scale-out links that form the densest connections in AI data centers demand higher reliability than traditional optics were designed to provide. Credo’s ALCs bring copper-class reliability to these links, enabling larger GPU clusters and higher-throughput connectivity for massive-scale AI deployments.” “As the speeds and distances required for AI exceed the capabilities of copper, there is a gap opening between copper cables and more expensive, power-hungry traditional pluggable optics," said Scott Wilkinson, Lead Analyst, Optical Components at Cignal AI. "Credo’s ZeroFlap ALC addresses this gap with a unique approach that provides row-scale reach while maintaining the reliability and low-cost benefits of AECs.” Credo’s 1.6T ZeroFlap active light cable (ALC) solution will be shipping in 2027. Today, at the OCP Global Summit, Credo President and CEO Bill Brennan will present “Wider. Slower. Better: Optics That Can Beat Copper” at 3:20 p.m. in room LL21DE of the San Jose Convention Center. Credo’s micro-emitter technology and its latest portfolio of copper and optical interconnect solutions will be demonstrated at the OCP Global Summit Expo Hall in Credo Booth B2, October 13-15, 2026. To request a meeting or product demo, please contact [email protected]. About Credo Credo’s mission is to transform connectivity at scale through fast, reliable, and energy-efficient system solutions. Our high-speed copper and optical interconnect technologies deliver industry-leading power and performance from chip to cluster to meet the ever-expanding data infrastructure demands of AI. Our vertically integrated connectivity portfolio is comprised of our flagship purple ZeroFlap (ZF) Active Electrical Cables (AECs) and ZF optical transceivers; optical components including silicon photonics-based photonic integrated circuits (SiPho PICs) and DSPs; OmniConnect AI memory and chip-to-chip interconnect; and retimers for Ethernet and PCIe—supported by our PILOT diagnostic and analytics software platform. Credo innovations enable our customers to connect the systems that connect the world. For more information, please visit https://www.credosemi.com. Follow Credo on LinkedIn. artigo.texto: Residents in an Indonesian data-center hub ran out of patience, and water, before officials did. On October 5, about 300 people in Batam blocked the road into Nongsa Digital Park, demanding the taps that had gone dry for months get turned back on. Protesters from the Sambau neighborhood, armed with empty jerry cans and plastic bottles, swarmed the compound's access road and refused to move. According to the Jakarta Post and the Star, residents said their piped water supply had been cut off, in some cases for three to six months, while the data centers next door kept running. One protester, Andi Lalang, put it plainly to reporters: since construction of the data center began, the neighborhood's water has been severely affected, and the supply has simply stopped. The anger wasn't sudden. This was the latest in a string of protests that had built over the previous two months, including a late-September demonstration at the Nongsa Special Economic Zone management office. Residents watched reservoir levels fall even as new server halls kept rising around them. A BP Batam official defused the immediate standoff. BP Batam is the state agency that runs the free-trade zone where Nongsa Digital Park sits, and the official promised piped water would be restored within two days, with six tanker trucks dispatched to deliver emergency supply. By Wednesday, water was back for roughly 53% of the affected households. For the other half, nothing had changed, and residents told local outlets they're ready to block the road again if the taps run dry a second time. BP Batam disputes the obvious reading. Denny Tondano, BP Batam's deputy for commercial affairs, denied that the data centers caused the shortage at all, pointing instead to a prolonged dry season driven by El Niño. That explanation runs into a problem of its own making. Local reports have described the data centers in Nongsa Digital Park as being served through a dedicated BP Batam pipeline connected to the Duriangkang Reservoir. The surrounding residential neighborhoods depend on the smaller Nongsa Reservoir instead - the one that's been running low. Two systems, two outcomes, same drought. The numbers ahead are the real warning. Nine data centers are planned or under construction in Nongsa Digital Park. Once they're all running, the complex will need roughly 285 megawatts of power and about 29 million liters of water a day, according to reporting compiled by Katadata and Earth Journalism Network. Combined with at least one additional large facility nearby, that adds up to something like 8.4% of Batam's entire water supply. All of it consumed by server cooling systems, in a city that can't yet guarantee piped water to the neighborhood next door. A single large AI data center can use up to 5 million gallons of water daily. That's roughly what a city of 10,000 to 50,000 people needs - which gives some sense of scale for what nine of them, fully built, would actually draw. Firmus has delayed its expected ASX IPO timetable after The Australian reported a major Nvidia partnership tied to a 360 megawatt AI factory in Batam, Indonesia. The deal could cover up to 170,000 Nvidia accelerators and support $US25 billion to $US30 billion in first-six-year revenue from committed offtake contracts. - Nvidia AI factory capacity building - ASX listing delayed for data center Batam has spent the last two years marketing itself as Southeast Asia's answer to Singapore's land-constrained data center market: close enough to Singapore for low-latency links, cheap enough on land and power to undercut it. Global Voices reported in April that the island's AI-ready data center boom has moved fast on approvals and slower on the utility planning that's supposed to back it up. The Jakarta Post has been tracking the strain since at least August. That's when it first reported that data center expansion in Batam was threatening both water and electricity supplies for ordinary residents - months before anyone blocked a road over it. None of this is abstract for the people who live there. Frankly, a resident who hasn't had running water in half a year doesn't much care whether El Niño or a new server farm caused it. They care that the facility across the street never seems to run dry. That's the actual story inside the AI infrastructure boom that doesn't show up in a chip shortage headline or a power purchase agreement: the water gets allocated first to the machines, and the humans wait for a tanker truck. Six trucks bought BP Batam two days of calm. The reservoir math behind nine data centers didn't go anywhere. artigo.texto: Rapidly rising computing density is pushing traditional systems to the limit. In particular, the demands for AI data center cooling are reshaping operating strategies. Rather than transitioning to liquid cooling data centers, operators are increasingly adopting hybrid cooling architectures that use liquid for the highest-density equipment while retaining efficient airflow to manage equipment cooling throughout facilities. Operators are looking to better understand data center fan efficiency. They are learning that advanced fans and rear-door heat exchangers combined with intelligent controls, monitoring, and adaptive operation can improve cooling performance while reducing energy consumption and freeing limited power resources for actual computing. Reliability is equally critical as cooling equipment must operate continuously under demanding conditions. Digital twins predictive maintenance can contribute to improved efficiency and increased uptime by better targeting maintenance and allowing operators to evaluate higher rack densities, cooling upgrades, and operating strategies before making capital investments. Finally, operators concerned about supply-chain risks are looking toward local-for-local manufacturing. Producing critical cooling equipment closer to customers can shorten lead times, reduce transportation and tariff risks, and provide regional manufacturing redundancy. Download AI Is Reshaping Data Center Cooling to see how hybrid cooling, smarter controls, digital modeling, and resilient supply chains can support scalable, long-term, efficient data center growth.

artigo.texto: Tower Semiconductor and Semtech Expand SiGe Partnership to Scale Power-Efficient Analog Connectivity for Data Centers Multi-year agreement expands dedicated capacity across Tower's global fab network to support the companies’ growth in optical and copper interconnects for next-generation AI infrastructure MIGDAL HAEMEK, Israel & CAMARILLO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 13, 2026-- Tower Semiconductor (Nasdaq/TASE: TSEM), the leading foundry for high-value analog semiconductor solutions, and Semtech Corporation (Nasdaq: SMTC), a leading provider of high-performance semiconductors powering AI data center networking and intelligent, connected Internet of Things ("IoT") devices worldwide, today announced an expanded multi-year agreement that builds on the companies’ 20-year partnership. Under the agreement, Semtech will invest in securing dedicated silicon germanium (SiGe) capacity at Tower in support of its strong design wins and demand for AI Data Center optical interconnect components. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261012105819/en/ AI’s next constraint is power, and a growing share of that power is spent moving data rather than computing it. As AI clusters scale across racks, rows and campuses, the energy cost of moving each bit is becoming central to how much useful work each accelerator can deliver. Each step in the speed roadmap, from 800G to 1.6T and on to 3.2T, raises the requirements for bandwidth, reach and power per bit, and increases the importance of the high-speed analog front end that drives and receives the signal. Semtech’s signal integrity portfolio, including transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs), modulator and laser drivers and linear equalizers, is built on Tower’s SiGe process technology and serves fully retimed optics (FRO), linear pluggable optics (LPO), linear receive optics (LRO), near-packaged optics (NPO), eXtra-dense pluggable optics (XPO), linear equalizers on PCB and active copper cables (ACC). Semtech believes that, together, these products position it to address copper links within the rack and optical links across the data center as the industry moves to its next generation of architectures. A testament to the results of the partnership is Semtech’s recent Optical Component Innovation (Chip/Wafer) award at the European Conference on Optical Communication (ECOC) 2026. The award recognizes Semtech’s 224 Gbps per Lane TIA Family for Linear Pluggable Optics built on Tower’s leading-edge SiGe technology. Tower and Semtech continue to work closely not only on capacity but also on joint technology roadmap designed to secure product leadership in multi-generational AI data center interconnects. The secured capacity spans Tower’s fabs in the United States, Israel and Japan, adding supply resilience and geographic diversification to Semtech’s manufacturing strategy. Building on current production, the agreement gives Semtech additional supply assurance as demand for its SiGe-based products is expected to grow across a broadening base of customer programs and end markets. “Connectivity is now a primary factor in how far AI systems can scale,” said Hong Hou, Semtech President and Chief Executive Officer. “Our customers are scaling interconnect bandwidth quickly and at massive scale. Meeting that demand requires long-term capacity planning and commitment with our manufacturing partners. Tower has been a trusted partner to Semtech for 20 years, and we are very pleased with our partnership agreement that secures dedicated SiGe capacity across three regions to grow across copper and optical interconnects, from 800G and 1.6T today through 3.2T and beyond.” “It is a source of profound satisfaction that our partnership with Semtech has grown so strong,” said Russell Ellwanger, Chief Executive Officer, Tower Semiconductor. “Together, we are driving truly accretive, platform-level solutions that help advance their designs delivering best-in-class figures of merit across present-generation, next-generation and N+2 technologies. By qualifying these solutions well ahead of market need, we both stand fully prepared for immediate implementation as the market moves into these generations. In doing so, we are the key drivers of the technologies carrying the market forward, ensuring a continual expansion of our already leading market share in optical transceiver connectivity within this high-growth market." For additional information about Tower’s SiGe and SiPho technology platforms, visit here. About Tower Semiconductor Tower Semiconductor Ltd. (NASDAQ/TASE: TSEM), the leading foundry of high-value analog semiconductor solutions, provides technology, development, and process platforms for its customers in growing markets such as consumer, industrial, automotive, mobile, infrastructure, medical and aerospace and defense. Tower Semiconductor focuses on creating a positive and sustainable impact on the world through long-term partnerships and its advanced and innovative analog technology offering, comprised of a broad range of customizable process platforms such as SiPho, SiGe, BiCMOS, mixed-signal/CMOS, RF CMOS, CMOS image sensor, non-imaging sensors, displays, and integrated power management (BCD and 700V). Tower Semiconductor also provides world-class design enablement for a quick and accurate design cycle as well as process transfer services including development, transfer, and optimization, to IDMs and fabless companies. To provide multi-fab sourcing and extended capacity for its customers, Tower Semiconductor currently owns one operating facility in Israel (200mm), two in the U.S. (200mm), and two in Japan (200mm and 300mm) which it owns through its 51% holdings in TPSCo and shares a 300mm facility in Agrate, Italy with STMicroelectronics. artigo.texto: Ultium Cells LLC, a joint venture between Detroit-based General Motors (GM) and South Korea’s LG Energy Solution, has announced a plan to produce lithium manganese-rich (LMR) prismatic battery cells at the GM manufacturing complex in Spring Hill, Tennessee. The Ultium partnership and EV battery production in the United States overall attracted investment momentum in the early 2020s as the administration of President Joe Biden offered incentives tied to EV sales and production. That momentum stalled significantly as the administration of President Donald J. Trump discontinued support measures for EVs and demonstrated a preference for fossil fuels and fossil fuel-consuming industry sectors. The shift in priorities also may have stalled momentum in the scaling up of U.S. EV battery recycling, including agreements reached by Ultium with battery materials recyclers and suppliers. Now, GM says it is “blazing a new trail in battery technology” at its Spring Hill complex near Nashville. The investment is “expected to make Ultium Cells the first manufacturer globally to commercially produce this next-generation technology, positioning GM at the forefront of bringing the technology to market in future electric vehicles.” GM says LMR prismatic battery cells mark a major step forward for the future of its EV sector, adding the technology is designed to offer energy density 33 percent greater compared with lithium-iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry but at a comparable cost. “Establishing LMR prismatic cell production at Ultium Cells in Spring Hill is a key step in our strategy to match the right battery technology to customer needs and strengthen our leadership in domestic battery manufacturing and innovation,” states GM. The automaker says high-nickel batteries will continue to give customers the highest range in its EV portfolio, while adding LMR positions the company to “leapfrog today’s more affordable chemistries and deliver lower costs with better performance.” According to GM, the manufacturing capabilities of Ultium Cells offers flexibility, with a planned ability to produce battery cells in multiple chemistries and form factors, helping tailor battery technology to the needs of different vehicles and applications. “Bringing this new battery cell to market first is a milestone moment for keeping America competitive globally in EV and battery technology leadership,” states GM. General Motors says construction and facility upgrades in Spring Hill will begin later this year and are expected to be completed in 2028. The expansion is projected to create 500 new jobs, joining the current workforce of 1,200 people.

artigo.texto: Bulgaria Raises Net Electricity Exports 62% on Solar Power and Battery Storage Net electricity exports have reached 3.5 TWh since January, driven by photovoltaics and storage. Industry group APSTE points to the lack of new wind capacity, as solar output declines in winter. Bulgaria's net electricity exports rose 62% from the start of the year to early October, reaching 3.5 TWh, compared with 2.16 TWh a year earlier. Renewable energy sources, supported by storage systems, are the main driver of the increase in output. According to grid operator ESO, the country is producing 12.24% more electricity, while consumption has risen 8.45%. Renewables drive the rise in output ESO data show renewable generation reaching 11.5 TWh, nearly 34% more than a year earlier. Renewable sources therefore account for almost 80% of the growth in the country's electricity output. In the region, Renalfa and Eurowind have inaugurated Tenevo, a 242 MWp solar complex with batteries, while Vojvodina has launched the environmental scoping phase for the Baranda solar plant. Storage deployment is advancing sharply. From the start of the year to 4 October, batteries delivered 1,720 GWh to the power system, compared with 190 GWh a year earlier, an increase of more than nine times. This storage allows cheap electricity produced during the day to be used in hours of high consumption and higher prices. A summer marked by heat and low Danube levels Prolonged heat and low Danube levels limited nuclear and hydropower generation in the region. Bulgaria nonetheless remained a net exporter and, during key periods, kept prices below those of neighboring markets. Industry group APSTE attributes this result to the combination of solar plants, batteries and the Kozloduy nuclear plant. On 8 October, the sixth reactor at Kozloduy was in planned maintenance and the fifth was running at reduced output because of the low Danube level. In the early afternoon, photovoltaic plants nonetheless produced close to 4,300 MW, more than national consumption of 4,100 MW. Batteries were charging at the same time at more than 4,000 MW to supply energy in the evening. Wind power remains stalled According to APSTE, solar output declines in winter while consumption rises. Since 2020, photovoltaic capacity has grown by about 600%, to nearly 7 GW, and storage systems are approaching 6 GW / 17 GWh. The association estimates investment in photovoltaics, batteries and related infrastructure at roughly â¬7 billion since 2020. Wind development, by contrast, has practically stopped. Bulgaria has only 716 MW of wind capacity and no new large wind farm has been built since 2013. By comparison, Romania has more than 3.5 GW and Greece more than 6 GW. Wind has a different daily and seasonal profile from solar and can deliver significant output in winter. - Gas44.1 % - Nuclear16.1 % - Coal15.7 % - Solar10.6 % - Wind8.3 % - Hydro3.5 % - Bioenergy0.9 % - Other fossil0.5 % - Other renewables0.4 % APSTE calls for easing administrative constraints Nikola Gazdov, chairman of APSTE, says solar power and batteries have significantly strengthened the country's energy security, but that this is not enough. He argues for attracting investment in wind power and says new capacity does not require subsidies, but clear rules and genuine easing of procedures. APSTE says Bulgaria could attract more than â¬4 billion in additional private investment in wind plants and storage systems by 2030. This outlook assumes that institutions provide predictable rules and remove administrative restrictions deemed unnecessary, including for projects located outside renewable acceleration zones.

artigo.texto: China is accelerating construction of massive data centers as competition with the United States over artificial intelligence continues to grow. A CNN report published October 13 highlights developments in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, where nearly 90 data center projects are planned. The area offers affordable land, access to renewable energy, and a climate that helps reduce cooling costs. The expansion is part of China’s broader effort to strengthen its AI infrastructure. Beijing has announced a $560 billion initiative covering computing and information systems over five years. China’s construction efforts also benefit from government coordination and fewer local development obstacles than some projects face in the United States. However, building more facilities does not automatically translate into greater computing capabilities. US export restrictions continue to limit Chinese companies’ access to advanced AI processors, while American technology firms maintain significant advantages in computing resources and investment. The growing demand for electricity also makes renewable energy an important consideration for both countries. China’s expansion illustrates how infrastructure, energy availability, and access to advanced technology have become central factors in the global AI competition.

This initiative is a critical step toward scaling locally made battery energy storage solutions that strengthen grid reliability, support renewable energy integration, and store energy for use during periods of high demand while helping ease supply-related energy costs. “For generations, manufacturing has been part of northern Illinois’ identity, and Richardson’s announcement demonstrates how that sector continues to shape our region’s economic future,” said ComEd President and CEO Gil Quiniones.“ComEd is committed to supporting business growth by making the grid investments needed to deliver industry-leading reliability at rates that are well below the average commercial and industrial rates for the top 20 largest metropolitan areas.” Richardson, a legacy manufacturer based in La Fox, is currently building the largest commercial battery storage system in Illinois. Its planned operational expansion will help scale the development and distribution of these products. Richardson is installing a 5-MWh research and development demonstration project, supported through the ComEd interconnection process. “Richardson Electronics has a long history of solving complex power and energy challenges through innovation and U.S.-based manufacturing,” said Greg Peloquin, Executive Vice President and General Manager of Power & Microwave Technologies and Green Energy Solutions groups. “Our advanced energy storage solutions will help customers manage energy more efficiently while supporting a more reliable and resilient grid. We value ComEd’s collaboration in bringing this onsite demonstration project to life.” The initiative is also supported by the Reimagining Energy and Vehicles in Illinois, or REV Illinois, program, which is helping Richardson Electronics strengthen its La Fox operations, advance energy technology manufacturing and support continued economic growth in Illinois. By storing electricity for use during periods of peak demand, battery storage can support a more resilient grid, integrate additional clean energy resources, and help ensure Illinois has the energy capacity needed to power future economic growth. “Safe, reliable and affordable energy is critical to the success of Illinois’ manufacturing sector and will require new generation, transmission investment and new technologies such as battery storage,” said Mark Denzler, President & CEO of the Illinois Manufacturers’ Association. “Richardson Electronics and ComEd’s announcement of a next-generation 5 MWh commercial battery storage system is a great example of manufacturing innovation and ingenuity that will help drive growth and economic development in Illinois.” Battery energy storage systems can charge when electricity is available and discharge when it is needed, helping customers manage energy use and support a more flexible electric system. Depending on how they are configured, batteries can also provide backup capabilities, reduce demand during peak periods, and support the integration of renewable energy resources. “When Kane County Commissioner Rick Williams and I first met with Richardson to discuss this project, I was immediately intrigued by both the economic and energy benefits the project could bring to the area and the state,” said State Representative Dan Ugaste (65th District). “Energy storage will be an important part of having affordable and reliable energy going forward. Seeing the value this project could bring, I was glad to help facilitate discussions with the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity to bring this project to fruition.” ComEd is supporting the project through its customer interconnection process and engineering studies. The company’s work includes helping prepare the site for the demonstration system and guiding Richardson through any potential system upgrade needs. This work will help to safely and reliably connect the demonstration system while maintaining service for surrounding customers. artigo.texto: Chinese challengers are flexing hard with cheap tech, big screens and ever-faster charging across a dizzying array of new EVs. But there’s one thing they can’t engineer, import or undercut, and that’s heritage. The French know it and that’s why Citroen brought back the 2CV name as a cut-price supermini, and now Peugeot is digging into its own sports car back catalogue. This one isn’t about cheap thrills, though. Revealed at the Paris motor show, the Peugeot RCZ Vision revives the cult RCZ coupe that was built between 2009 and 2015. It revives the name with a potent 368kW electric powertrain, a solid-state battery and a 1000-volt architecture. The French have come out firing at the 2026 Paris motor show, seemingly doubling their efforts in the new car space and the headline numbers for Peugeot’s reborn sports coupe, the RCZ, are serious. Peugeot claims 500 horsepower, which is about 368kW. It also claims up to 600km of driving range and a target energy consumption of 11.5kWh/100km on the WLTP cycle. The efficiency figure is still to be confirmed but that’s a frugal number for something this quick and powerful. Peugeot hasn’t given a battery capacity but something around the 70kWh realm appears to line up with the maths. The solid-state cells were developed with Factorial Energy, an American energy technology company based in Massachusetts. It’s currently developing next-gen solid-state battery technology for EVs, aerospace and even defence. The battery cell pack is claimed to be just 110mm thick and that thin pack is the main reason the roofline sits so low. The Peugeot RCZ Vision rides on a platform based on Stellantis’ new STLA One architecture, which goes into production under the next E-208 in 2027. Stellantis had previously talked about 800-volt electrics and LFP batteries for STLA One but the RCZ Vision steps that up to 1000 volts, which is what allows the 10-minute fast-charge claim. The tech gets even more interesting inside. Peugeot calls its approach ‘X-by-Wire’. The steering wheel has no mechanical connection to the front wheels and the steering ratio changes with speed. The Hypersquare control looks like a tray-table with cupholders turned on its side, and Peugeot reckons it turns slightly less than one full rotation from lock to lock, making it super direct. Conventional steering wheels takes about three turns lock to lock, give or take. Brake-by-wire also replaces the hydraulic link between the pedal and the brakes, which Peugeot says makes regenerative braking smoother. Level 2++ hands-free driving is also on board. Peugeot has bucked the screen-count arms race by fitting transparent Micro LED displays and the central screen can be switched off completely so it virtually disappears from view. “With Peugeot RCZ Vision, we are setting out our vision with a car firmly focused on the future, dedicated to delivering the ultimate driving pleasure,” said Peugeot CEO Alain Favey. There are plenty of nods to the original car too. The ‘double-bubble’ glass roof and the active rear spoiler both return and the forged wheels measure 21 inches at the front and 22 inches at the rear. Unlike the original, the RCZ Vision has a four-seat cabin that Peugeot says can carry two adults comfortably in the back. Peugeot hasn’t committed to building the RCZ and two-door coupes are a niche segment these days. The original RCZ’s old rival, the Audi TT, is reportedly due for an electric comeback, though, so you shouldn’t rule out a production version just yet. Even if this exact car never reaches showrooms, much of what’s underneath it will. Peugeot is one of four Stellantis brands sharing 70 per cent of the group’s future investment. The STLA One hardware, steer-by-wire and L2++ tech will spread across the wider Stellantis line-up, starting with the next Peugeot E-208.

artigo.texto: Jakarta (ANTARA) - The government is determined to ensure that carbon trading generates significant economic benefits for local communities, especially those actively involved in environmental restoration efforts, Indonesian Environment Minister Jumhur Hidayat said. He underscored the importance of enabling grassroots communities, indigenous peoples, and local residents to reap economic gains from carbon trading during a technical guidance session on carbon economic value and climate-resilient low-carbon development for regional leaders in Jakarta on Tuesday. Hidayat stressed that the government is working to ensure that carbon trading creates opportunities not only for major investors but also for residents directly connected to natural ecosystems that require restoration and conservation. The minister noted that the extent of benefits received by communities could serve as a measure of the integrity of carbon trading activities in Indonesia. He further emphasized that the equitable distribution of economic benefits is one of the key indicators of a high-integrity carbon market. For example, he pointed to the economic potential of mangrove restoration, which can absorb around 3,000 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent per hectare annually. Assuming each carbon credit is valued at between US$50 and US$60, he added, a hectare of mangroves could generate an estimated value of around US$150,000. He went on to say that a mangrove restoration project could also help strengthen community empowerment efforts, as it would typically require workers over a period of three to four years. Hidayat described the carbon economy as a more responsible development approach, stressing the need to move away from conventional models that often drive economic growth at the expense of environmental sustainability and social equity. The government, he added, views the new approach as a way to position carbon trading as a scheme that supports environmental restoration while generating tangible economic benefits for local communities. artigo.texto: O evento ocorre em um contexto de forte crescimento contínuo da demanda por eletricidade no Vietnã, impulsionado pelo crescimento industrial e por uma onda de investimentos em centros de dados de inteligência artificial (AIDCs). A Trinasolar lança o sistema de painéis solares e armazenamento de energia Vertex N G3 TOPCon 3.0. A Trinasolar, uma das empresas líderes mundiais em energia solar e soluções inteligentes de armazenamento de energia, lançou recentemente o painel solar Vertex N G3 TOPCon 3.0 (até 760W) e o sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) Elementa 3 de 6,25MWh em um evento realizado na cidade de Ho Chi Minh. O Vertex N G3 foi desenvolvido na plataforma de tecnologia de células fotovoltaicas TOPCon 3.0 da Trinasolar, apresentando quatro avanços tecnológicos principais. A tecnologia da plataforma de células fotovoltaicas Ultra aumenta a potência e a eficiência bifacial. As tecnologias de corte múltiplo e passivação de borda reduzem as perdas de corrente, ao mesmo tempo que melhoram a eficiência sob sombreamento parcial e minimizam o fenômeno de pontos quentes. A tecnologia de encapsulamento de ultra-alta densidade aumenta a eficiência e a potência de saída do módulo. O coeficiente de bifacialidade atinge 85% ± 5%, permitindo que o módulo utilize radiação adicional da face posterior em condições adequadas. O coeficiente de temperatura de potência de -0,26%/°C ajuda a limitar a degradação de potência quando operando em altas temperaturas, sendo adequado para o clima quente do Vietnã. A degradação máxima de potência é de 0,35% ao ano a partir do segundo ano e é garantida por 30 anos, proporcionando aos desenvolvedores de projetos uma base mais sólida para estimar a produção de eletricidade e a eficiência do projeto a longo prazo. A Trina Storage também apresentou o Elementa 3, um sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) de grande escala com capacidade de 6,25 MWh, utilizando células de bateria de 587 Ah desenvolvidas pela Trinasolar. O Elementa 3 apoia a integração de fontes de energia renováveis e aumenta a flexibilidade na operação do sistema elétrico, incluindo projetos conectados à rede, à medida que o Vietnã continua a expandir a energia solar para atender à crescente demanda das indústrias e centros de dados. O armazenamento de energia também está recebendo crescente atenção no planejamento de desenvolvimento energético do Vietnã. De acordo com o Plano de Desenvolvimento Energético VIII revisado, o Vietnã pretende desenvolver de 10.000 a 16.300 MW de capacidade de armazenamento de energia em baterias até 2030, o equivalente a aproximadamente 5,5% a 6,9% da capacidade total de geração de energia do país. O plano também orienta a implantação de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) em áreas próximas a fontes de energia renovável ou grandes centros de consumo para dar suporte à operação do sistema elétrico. O projeto integrado de energia solar e armazenamento de energia da Trinasolar no Corona Resort em Phu Quoc é um exemplo da aplicação prática de soluções fotovoltaicas e de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) no Vietnã.

artigo.texto: “Kerthi Bhumi Satwika is not merely a place name, but a reflection of a broader shift in Bali’s development approach,” he said in a statement on Saturday (October 10). Koster said the six designated low-emission areas are Ubud, the Nusa Penida Islands, Nusa Dua, Kuta, Sanur, and the Gajah Mada Cultural Heritage Area in Denpasar. Each area has its own characteristics and priorities, he said. Ubud focuses on cultural and environmental tourism, while Nusa Penida emphasizes preserving the island's ecosystem. Meanwhile, Nusa Dua, Kuta, and Sanur are expected to promote the consistent adoption of environmentally friendly tourism practices. The Gajah Mada Cultural Heritage Area in Denpasar, meanwhile, aims to integrate historical preservation with sustainable urban development. Koster said the designation aims to align spatial planning policies with efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and accelerate the adoption of clean energy across sectors. “We must ensure that economic and tourism development go hand in hand with environmental protection and the long-term sustainability of local communities,” he said. The low-emission area policy was also developed in response to Bali's increasingly complex development challenges, ranging from transportation and mobility to climate change, the governor added. The program is built around five strategic pillars: Green Energy, Green Transportation, Green Ecosystems, Green Tourism Industry, and Green Society. Through these pillars, the Bali provincial government seeks to reduce emissions from the energy, transportation, and tourism sectors, as well as through waste management at the source. Koster emphasized that the program's success depends on consistent implementation and strong cross-sectoral coordination. The initiative also calls for active collaboration among various tourism businesses, traditional villages, local communities, research institutions, and the wider public. He added that the program aligns with Bali's development vision, Nangun Sat Kerthi Loka Bali, and the principles of local wisdom embodied in Sad Kerthi. It is also consistent with the Future Bali Development Guidelines and the 100-Year Bali New Era roadmap for 2025–2125. artigo.texto: ZTE's David An Shares TCO-Optimized AI Factory Vision ZTE Expert David AN Shares TCO-Optimized AI Factory Vision at Data Centre World Singapore 2026 October 12, 2026 Sponsored by ZTE SINGAPORE, September 30, 2026, at Data Centre World (DCW) Singapore 2026, David AN, Director of ZTE CTO Group, delivered a keynote titled "From Data Center to AI Factory, TCO-Optimized AIDC" in the DCW Keynote Theatre. The presentation outlined how the explosive growth of AI is transforming data centers from traditional facilities into integrated AI factories, and why the industry must optimize the entire AI factory lifecycle - not individual components—to achieve sustainable total cost of ownership (TCO). AN opened by highlighting the rapid acceleration of global computing demand. Inference now drives 70% of intelligent computing growth, while global daily token usage has increased by 1,000 times in just two years. By 2032, global data center scale is projected to reach 246 GW, with AI data centers (AIDC) accounting for 52% of that capacity. This surge is placing unprecedented pressure on power, cooling, architecture, and deployment. "AI is pushing traditional data center architecture to its limits," said David AN. "The industry must restructure power systems to dynamically match load demand, reduce transmission loss, and rethink how compute, power, and cooling work together. " The presentation identified three industry trends: 1. Power Becomes the New Bottleneck. Data center power is evolving from a single grid input to multi-energy synergy and generation-storage-distribution-consumption linkage. The system must match power with computing load in real time across day/hour, hour, minute, second, and millisecond levels. Technologies such as 800V HVDC, solid-state transformers (SST), and multi-level energy storage are essential. 2. Cooling Must Follow Compute Density. Low-density data halls (≤40 kW) can rely on air cooling with PUE ≤1.25. High-density halls (60–240 kW) require air-liquid hybrid cooling with PUE ≤1.15. Ultra-high-density AI halls (≥600 kW) demand full liquid cooling with PUE ≤1.09. Cooling must evolve alongside chip and rack trends to support the next generation of AI workloads. 3. AI Infrastructure Must Evolve at GPU Speed. Traditional site-assembled construction is too slow. The industry is moving toward modularity and prefabrication, full-unit transport, on-site assembly, and joint commissioning. With 90% MEP modularization, delivery periods can be reduced by 50%. This approach also enables phased investment, synchronized power and cooling matching, and sustained technology roadmap evolution. ZTE's vision is to optimize the AI factory as one system that integrates the co-design and coordination of computing, power, and cooling. This system is characterized by synergy management, energy saving, flexible adaptability, and rapid delivery. ZTE's end-to-end AI infrastructure capabilities span power, cooling, and prefabricated data centers. Key solutions include 800V HVDC power modules, safe lithium batteries, intelligent busbars, cold-plate and immersion liquid cooling, fan walls, and fully prefabricated data centers. With more than 20 countries, 500+ cases, 400,000 cabinets, more than 3,200MW, and 3.5 million square meters of delivered projects, ZTE has established itself as a leading end-to-end data center solution provider. Since entering the modular data center field in 2009, the company has continuously advanced prefabricated and green data center technologies, solidifying its competitive position in the global data center market. About the Author: David AN, ZTE Expert

artigo.texto: South Korea plans to launch its Global Verified Carbon Market (GVCM) in 2027, establishing a framework for issuing and trading carbon credits generated by overseas greenhouse gas reduction projects. The initiative will allow eligible credits to be traded on the Korea Exchange and potentially used for corporate environmental, social and governance (ESG) activities and national emissions reduction commitments. Deputy Prime Minister and Economy and Finance Minister Lee Hyung-il chaired a meeting of economic ministers in Seoul on October 12, where the government finalized the detailed implementation plan. The framework builds on a roadmap announced in December 2025 and outlines the market’s operating structure, credit verification requirements and governance arrangements. A central feature of the GVCM will be the selective use of blockchain technology to record critical carbon credit information, including project operators, emissions reduction volumes, unique identification numbers and approved methodologies. Other information will remain in conventional databases, creating a dual-track system intended to balance data integrity, operational efficiency and system stability. Carbon Credits to Trade Through Korea Exchange Initially, the government will issue credits in standard electronic form for trading through South Korea’s voluntary carbon market exchange. Authorities will consider introducing digital asset-based issuance alongside conventional credits as market activity develops, taking into account trading volumes, regulatory developments and investor confidence. The government has also renamed the initiative from the Global Voluntary Carbon Market to the Global Verified Carbon Market. The revised designation reflects its intention to accommodate credits that qualify for use in both voluntary corporate initiatives and regulated emissions reduction programs. The framework establishes two credit categories based on whether the country hosting an emissions reduction project authorizes the international transfer of the resulting credits. GVCM A credits will receive host-country authorization and may qualify for regulatory purposes, including national climate commitments under the Paris Agreement and the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA). They may also support corporate ESG initiatives. GVCM NA credits, which lack the required authorization, will initially be restricted to voluntary corporate environmental activities. These credits could subsequently be upgraded to GVCM A status if the host country grants the necessary approval and corresponding adjustments. South Korea is also evaluating whether GVCM credits could eventually be integrated into its domestic emissions trading system or greenhouse gas target management framework. Any such integration would depend on verification standards, compliance with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement and applicable domestic legal requirements. Governance Framework to Include Developing Countries The proposed issuing organization will comprise a board of directors, a technical oversight committee and a secretariat. The board, representing participating countries, will establish policy direction and supervise technical governance. The technical committee will oversee matters such as credit issuance, while the secretariat will manage issuance procedures, credit records and registry operations. The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is serving as the interim secretariat. A dedicated secretariat is expected to be established when the market officially launches. The governance structure is designed to give developing countries a greater role in decision-making while respecting their sovereignty over emissions baselines, operating rules and sustainable development priorities. Eligible project categories will reflect participating countries’ development needs and South Korea’s technological capabilities. Potential initiatives include mangrove restoration, agricultural waste management, methane capture and energy efficiency improvements. The government is also discussing cooperation with international institutions, including the World Bank and the Green Climate Fund, to convert emissions reductions from existing projects into GVCM credits. International Carbon Market Growth Drives Strategy International carbon trading is attracting greater attention as countries seek additional ways to meet their Paris Agreement commitments. Many governments face difficulties achieving their 2030 nationally determined contributions through domestic emissions reductions alone. However, inconsistent standards and concerns about the environmental effectiveness of some credits have raised questions about the credibility of international carbon markets. South Korea sees an opportunity to address these concerns through a standardized system combining verification, traceability, and clear rules governing credit eligibility. Projections from MSCI cited in the government’s assessment indicate that the carbon credit market could reach $7 billion to $35 billion by 2030 and $45 billion to $250 billion by 2050. To attract participants, South Korea plans to work with GGGI through international networks, including the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework and the Asia-Pacific Carbon Market Roundtable. At the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, scheduled for November 2026, the government intends to pursue letters of intent with interested countries. A climate investment forum planned for December will further promote the initiative. The government aims to identify priority project sectors during 2026, establish the issuing body in 2027, and finalize project structures before beginning full-scale operations. The GVCM is intended to strengthen confidence in cross-border carbon credits while creating a framework through which verified emissions reductions can support corporate climate initiatives and eligible national targets.

artigo.texto: Damion Smy Toyota agrees to $750 million HiLux, Prado DPF class action settlement 9 Hours Ago Deputy News Editor The Peugeot RCZ Vision has been revealed at the 2026 Paris motor show, with the French brand saying the sleek electric coupe concept previews the look of its future models both inside and out, as well as groundbreaking technology including solid-state batteries. A follow-on from the original petrol-powered RCZ coupe, based on the Peugeot 308 hatch and sold in Australia between 2010 and 2015, the four-seat RCZ Vision concept wraps the brand's upcoming technologies in its 'Feline Future' design language. This includes advanced solid-state battery tech, which promises to be safer and cost less than conventional lithium-ion batteries, as well as being much faster to charge and offer between 20 and 50 per cent longer range per charge. While not confirmed as a production model, the RCZ Vision teams a 1000V electrical architecture with Peugeot's higher-density, space-saving solid-state battery tech. This enables a 500hp (373kW) power output, yet with low claimed energy consumption of just 11.5kWh/100km, with the automaker targeting a 600km WLTP range from a battery pack that's only 110mm thick. Developed with US battery firm Factorial Energy, with which Peugeot parent company Stellantis entered an agreement in 2021, the solid-state battery enables a claimed 10-80 per cent charge in as little as 10 minutes. Beyond its battery tech, the RCZ Vision shows off Peugeot's upcoming design principles, which include an aggressive, muscular stance and new three-claw headlights, also seen on the E-T16 concept revealed in Paris, as well as three-claw tail-lights and an active rear spoiler. Massive 21-inch front and 22-inch rear forged aluminium alloy wheels complement its aggressive haunches, including triangular details in a nod to the original RCZ, while another reference to the original is the double-bubble roof design, which sits above a transparent glass cockpit. The cabin includes the 'Hypersquare' steering wheel seen in the E-T16, along with the 2025 Polygon and the 2023 Inception concepts. The Hypersquare wheel has been confirmed as a feature on the production version of the next-generation 208 hatchback, which is expected to be revealed in 2027, with the 2008 small SUV expected to follow. The RCZ Vision features variable-ratio steer-by-wire steering, reducing driver hand movements at low speeds while adjusting for smoother steering at higher speeds. The RCZ Vision is also the first Peugeot to use brake-by-wire technology, which replaces the conventional hydraulic connection between the brake pedal and calipers with electronic controls. Peugeot says this brings more precise braking modulation and greater efficiency through improved integration of regenerative braking. The Hypersquare steering wheel is teamed with the latest version of Peugeot's i-Cockpit, featuring transparent micro-LED displays positioning configurable data directly in the driver's field of vision, as well as a floating central display angled towards the driver. The recycled-leather-trimmed seats are asymmetrical and offer additional support towards the centre of the vehicle, while the centre console features physical machined-aluminium controls arranged on a piece of frosted glass. Space efficiency measures include movable air vents, which can be stowed when not in use, while a Serica analogue clock forms part of the cabin design. Peugeot's multiple concepts at its home motor show come as the French brand receives greater attention from parent company Stellantis. Earlier this year, Peugeot was named as one of four priority brands by Stellantis, alongside Jeep, Ram and Fiat, ahead of other marques in its stable including Alfa Romeo, Chrysler and Citroën. This bodes well for its future in Australia, after local importer Inchcape, which also distributes brands including Subaru, Deepal and Foton here, announced it would hand back the local Peugeot distribution rights it has held since 2017. A new Australian importer is yet to be officially announced and nor has Stellantis resumed local Citroën distribution following Inchcape's decision to cease distributing the smaller French brand in 2024, ending 102 years of sales in Australia. artigo.texto: Renewable energy producer R.Power is nearing completion of its first utility-scale BESS project in Romania, the 127MW / 254 MWh Scornicesti BESS. EPC contractor Parapet, working with R.Power’s in-house EPC management team, commenced construction in spring 2026. It has, over the past three months, laid foundations and deployed all 46 battery units and 23 containerised medium-voltage transformer stations. Scornicesti BESS will be one of the first assets of its kind in Romania, and one of the largest BESS assets to enter operation in Central & Eastern Europe (CEE). Connecting Scornicesti directly to the high-voltage national transmission grid, operated by Transelectrica, is a major undertaking that goes well beyond a standard project and has required extensive design works. Once connected, expected in late 2026/early 2027, the project will become a strategic energy asset for Romania’s national energy system. R.Power secured a €46 million financing package for the project in June 2026. Under the terms of the deal, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) provided €44 million in investment and bridge financing, while Polish development bank Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego (BGK) issued a €2.3 million bank guarantee to secure the long-term optimisation contract in place with regional trading partner GEN-I. The project, located in Olt County, is co-owned through a JV with France’s Eiffel Investment Group. “As a utility-scale asset connected to the national transmission grid, Scornicesti BESS will actively support the stabilisation of Romania’s energy system.” said Florin Federenciuc, R.Power Country Head for Romania. “By integrating BESS at the heart of its energy transition, Romania is strengthening its grid resilience and supporting the roll-out of renewable energy generation. Having contracted our first Romanian PV assets just two years ago, we are proud to now be playing this vital role in one of Europe’s fastest growth energy transition markets. “Together with EBRD, BGK, Eiffel Investment Group and GEN-I, we look forward to completing the final phase of construction and commissioning and getting this strategic asset to work”. Scornicesti BESS forms part of one of Central and Eastern Europe’s largest utility-scale energy storage pipelines. R.Power’s BESS portfolio in operations and under construction in CEE currently stands at 0.9 GW / 3 GWh, with an additional 0.7 GW / 2.8 GWh of commercialised, ready-to-build projects.

artigo.texto: Peugeot RCZ Vision previews a solid-state battery and 1000V charging Peugeot RCZ Vision is a 500 hp concept with a 110 mm solid-state battery, up to 600 km of range and 10–80% charging in 10 minutes. A 110 mm-thick solid-state battery, 500 hp and a 10–80% charge in ten minutes: Peugeot has presented an unusual continuation of the RCZ story. The RCZ Vision remains a concept and brand manifesto, but it showcases design and technologies Peugeot links to its future models. The key feature is a 1000V electrical architecture and solid-state battery cells developed with Factorial Energy. The concept uses an architecture based on the STLA One platform. Peugeot quotes up to 600 km of range and a target combined WLTP energy consumption of 11.5 kWh/100 km. The company explicitly says that consumption figure still has to be confirmed. The original RCZ is referenced by the sports-coupe format and its distinctive double-bubble roof. The new car is far more futuristic, with a low silhouette, pronounced fenders, a transparent upper body section and an active rear spoiler that deploys while driving. Inside, there is a Hypersquare control and Steer-by-Wire with no mechanical steering connection to the wheels. RCZ Vision is also Peugeot’s first model to demonstrate Brake-by-Wire electronic brake control. The concept differs from the former coupe by much more than the absence of a petrol engine. Peugeot presents RCZ Vision as a showcase for solid-state batteries, a 1000V architecture, X-by-Wire technologies and a new generation of the i-Cockpit driver interface. Peugeot has not announced a production date, a final production specification or a price. It is therefore too early to call RCZ Vision a confirmed return of the RCZ to showrooms: for now, the company has revived the idea of the coupe as a concept and shown technologies that could reach future Peugeot models.

artigo.texto: PHOENIX — Gov. Katie Hobbs and her Republican opponent, U.S. Rep. Andy Biggs, have one thing they can agree on: data centers. Both reject calls for a moratorium on new data centers proposed by Attorney General Kris Mayes, with Hobbs saying it’s not the right approach. "I think there are places where data centers make sense, and they're an important part of the high-tech economy that we're growing here,” she told reporters last month. Biggs agrees. After last week’s gubernatorial debate, he said local communities should have the final say. “There are many who don't want them at all, and others that are willing to investigate and are thinking about getting them,” he said. Do you have a concern in your community or a news tip? We want to hear from you! Connect with us: share@abc15.com He pointed to Marana’s decision to approve a data center after Tucson’s city council rejected a proposal for a Project Blue facility, saying “the company’s moving to Marana.” However, the Marana facility is one of up to three sites Project Blue’s developer, Beale Infrastructure, is working on. The company moved the proposed Tucson facility to just outside the city, in an unincorporated part of Pima County, after the city rejected the project. Biggs and Hobbs both say Arizona needs state standards for water and power use at data centers. “That data centers pay for themselves,” Hobbs said. “That they're not raising utility costs on Arizonans. That they're using water sustainably, and that they're addressing real and valid community concerns about data centers in neighborhoods.” She pushed for the repeal of state tax incentives for data centers – a tax break she voted for when she was a lawmaker in the state Senate. Hobbs negotiated a three-year moratorium on the incentives in this year’s budget with legislative Republicans. “We landed in a good place, and we can still have conversations about the water use, the energy use,” Hobbs said in July. Biggs, who voted against the incentives when he was in the Senate, said he wants to get rid of them permanently if elected governor. “Well, the first thing we're going to do is, we're not going to provide taxpayer subsidies or incentives for data centers to come in here,” he said. Biggs said he’s met with industry leaders and told them they don’t need the incentives. “I haven't had anybody say that they would leave without those incentives or with the constraints that I've proposed,” he said. Biggs has proposed developers pay for all the needed infrastructure and that data centers not “encroach on current and future natural growth of water and energy policy.” Hobbs, who has said she still supports a repeal of the tax breaks, said the current three-year freeze on new applications is an opportunity to craft a data-center policy. "I understand that many Arizonans are worried about data centers, and we want to make sure we're addressing those concerns in the right way,” she said. Meanwhile, Mayes is holding a town hall in Mesa on Oct. 14 to discuss her proposed statewide moratorium on new data centers. “We need a temporary ban,” she told reporters after last month's attorney general debate. “We need a pause so that we can get our hands around this situation.” Mayes said she’s working on a plan for a new approval process that would allow communities to vote on data center projects and create a commission to review proposed data centers like the Arizona Power Plant and Transmission Line Siting Committee does for energy projects.

artigo.texto: Maxxen Day 2026 welcomed energy industry executives, investors, project developers, technology companies and business partners from all across the European continent, from the UK to Türkiye. Maxxen Energy’s factory in Ayd?n, Türkiye, opened in December 2025. In just nine months, the company has delivered more than 600 MWh across 20+ projects, reaching nearly 5% of the European grid-scale BESS market. Maxxen believes this makes it the fastest-growing European BESS manufacturer ever. At the event, Maxxen also announced its membership of SolarPower Europe. The future of Europe’s energy storage market took centre stage Sessions explored the technology landscape, market dynamics and revenue outlook for Europe’s energy storage market. Panels looked at how to finance the investments needed to meet the growing demand for flexibility, and at the role of risk management and insurance in securing that financing. Project developers shared what they learned moving from their first projects to large-scale portfolios, and the challenges of scaling. Sessions and panels featuring international companies including Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, Wood Mackenzie, Clean Horizon, Solas Capital, Volteo Capital, Gresham House, Munich Re, Zagope, Luxera and Crowmie brought perspectives from across the BESS value chain. “We are shaping the future of the industry, together” Ruben Valiente, Managing Director of Maxxen Energy, said: “At Maxxen Day we opened our factory in Türkiye to the European battery storage industry and showed what we believe is one of the most advanced BESS factories in Europe. We also believe Maxxen is the fastest-growing European BESS manufacturer ever, with more than 600 MWh delivered in just nine months. artigo.texto: The News Despite increasingly critical media coverage of AI and the spread of data centers across the US, one news network has been painting a more positive picture. More than half of the references to data centers on Fox News over the last two years would have left viewers with a favorable impression, compared to less than 10% on CNN and 5% on MS NOW, according to a new Semafor analysis of mentions of data centers on each network. The mentions were pulled from closed captions preserved by the Internet Archive, which keeps a digital, searchable library of recorded TV news. A pair of AI models from Anthropic and OpenAI scored each reference on its content, with the networkâs name removed. Mentions of data centers have, predictably, shot up across all three networks in recent months as political backlash against AI swells and the data centers themselves have become a salient issue ahead of the midterms. But Foxâs opinion and morning shows, including My View with Lara Trump, Fox & Friends, and Life, Liberty & Levin, leaned on the promise of AI, economic investment and the race with China, skewing Foxâs coverage more favorably, the analysis showed. The networkâs news shows were more measured. In an Aug. 23 monologue that at one point featured a chyron reading âThe case for data centers,â Fox host Brian Kilmeade acknowledged âreal concerns,â but argued that âsaying no to data centers nationwide also means saying no to the tax dollars that can flow into a community. â¦ If Americans donât build the infrastructure to meet the demand, somebody else will.â On CNN and MS NOW, the criticism focused as much on the facilitiesâ political toxicity as on harms like power bills or water use, casting them as unpopular with voters and a liability for politicians who back them heading into the midterms. Data centers âare driving up energy costs, sucking up water supplies, wiping out rather than creating jobs,â MS NOWâs Katy Tur said in May. âPoliticians beware.â Polling shows that across demographic groups, Americans hold increasingly negative views of data centers: More than half of Americans say data centers are mostly bad for the environment, Pew Research Center found last month, compared with 39% in January. Fox News did not comment for this story. In this article: Maxâs view The pro-data center programming on Fox News comes as the right tries to define its positions in an AI-fueled, post-Donald Trump future. Foxâs favorable data center coverage mirrors Trumpâs position on their growth and the need for AI companies to help fuel the US economy. âThe only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor,â Trump wrote on Truth Social in August. âIf we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame.â But anger about data centers and the rapid advancement of AI represents a faultline within the MAGA coalition that swept Trump back into office. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis and Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., have questioned some data centers in their states, while Texas Gov. Greg Abbott seems to have flipped from supporting data centers to looking to slow their growth in his state amid a tougher-than-expected reelection campaign. Some on the right I have talked to in the last several months worry that Fox News, which Trump watches religiously, and other pro-data center voices are encouraging the president to take positions that are broadly unpopular with his rural and suburban base. âThe Big Tech oligarchs, the guys driving AI, did a terrible job,â Steve Bannon, a staunchly anti-AI Trump ally, told the Daily Signal in September. âThey came in to try to muscle local communities, and particularly since President Trumpâs strongest base is in exurban and rural communities, thatâs where they were really the ugliest, and they havenât made their case, and they particularly havenât made their case at the local level about the economics of this, and the energy of this, and the water of this, and the manifestation of what these things are going to be used for.â Room for Disagreement Not all of Foxâs data center coverage has been rosy; its tenor grew slightly less favorable in 2026 compared to last year. âItâs taxing our system way too much on water, agriculture land, or electricity. Weâre gonna implode,â the Texas agriculture commissioner said in an interview on a weekend Fox show in August. âWe just canât do it. Thereâs not enough.
