artigo.texto: Land & Expand: North America's Data Center Pipeline Expands Under Pressure Key Highlights - Large-scale projects like Fluidstack's 1.5 GW AI data center in Texas exemplify the industry's move toward industrial-scale infrastructure supporting advanced computing needs. - Community opposition and regulatory scrutiny are increasingly influencing project approvals, as seen in Mahomet, Illinois, where public opposition halted negotiations. - Developers are securing land, power, and water infrastructure while addressing local concerns about environmental impact, noise, and costs, reflecting a more complex development environment. - Major tech companies like Microsoft, Google, and AWS are expanding their regional footprints with multi-phase campuses, often integrating renewable energy and onsite generation. - The data center pipeline remains robust, with projects at various stages—from land acquisition to construction—highlighting ongoing industry growth despite rising development challenges. Land & Expand is Data Center Frontier's periodic look at the latest data center development news, including new sites, land acquisitions and campus expansions across North America. This latest installment finds the development pipeline continuing to expand, even as the requirements for bringing large-scale projects online grow more complicated. Developers are securing land, planning new power infrastructure and advancing campuses measured in hundreds of megawatts or more. At the same time, local governments and residents are demanding greater clarity on electricity costs, water consumption, noise, tax incentives and the long-term effects of industrial-scale computing facilities. A succession of development disclosures and project milestones through September and early October 2026 illustrates both the geographical reach of North America's expanding data center pipeline and the growing difficulty of measuring how much proposed capacity will ultimately be delivered. The projects range from preliminary discussions and newly secured development sites to campuses already under construction. Some are advancing through formal permitting and power studies; others remain contingent on customers, financing or local approvals. Together, they reveal an industry still expanding aggressively, but operating under increasingly complex development conditions. Fluidstack: Cameron County, Texas — Up to 1.5 GW One of the largest newly disclosed projects is Fluidstack's AI data center development in Cameron County in the Rio Grande Valley. The project surfaced publicly September 10 when Cameron County announced that it had issued Fluidstack a worksite permit for property near Harlingen. The permit authorizes preliminary site work, including grading, utilities and related infrastructure, rather than construction of the data center buildings themselves. Fluidstack subsequently disclosed considerably more detail on September 21, saying construction had begun on a $4 billion first phase capable of supporting as much as 1.5 GW. Fluidstack expects the project to generate more than 2,500 construction jobs and several hundred permanent positions. The company has placed unusual emphasis on the project's local infrastructure impact. It says it requested no local property-tax abatements and intends to pay for the energy, water and infrastructure necessary to serve the campus. Cooling will use a recirculating closed-loop system. At up to 1.5 GW in its announced first phase, Cameron County represents a major addition to the Texas AI development pipeline, reflecting the increasingly industrial scale of projects designed to support advanced computing. Microsoft ATL50: Union City, Georgia A new filing for Microsoft's ATL50 campus entered Georgia's Development of Regional Impact review process on September 15. Microsoft filed plans for ATL50, a new data center campus at 5235 Stonewall Tell Road in Union City, southwest of Atlanta. Plans call for two three-story data center buildings totaling approximately 910,000 square feet on 88 acres. The filing projects completion in 2032. Microsoft already has a substantial Georgia footprint, with development activity in Fairburn, Douglasville, Palmetto, Rome, East Point and other communities. ATL50 represents another proposed campus in the greater Atlanta market rather than entry into a new region. No electrical capacity has been disclosed. Project Gravel: Pima County, Arizona Another proposed development emerged through public-records reporting rather than a corporate announcement. Documents obtained in September disclosed Project Gravel, an eight-building data center campus being evaluated on approximately 160 acres of vacant land in unincorporated Pima County west of Sahuarita, Arizona. Plans show eight buildings of roughly 203,000 square feet each, producing a potential campus of approximately 1.6 million square feet, along with a dedicated electrical substation, roads and parking infrastructure. Project documents contemplate full buildout by 2029, contingent on the development advancing through the necessary approvals. County staff had reportedly been evaluating the proposal for months before details became public. Neither the developer nor a prospective tenant has been publicly identified, and the planned electrical load remains undisclosed. The disclosure has already generated local concern: Residents gathered September 29 to discuss the project's potential effects on water, energy use and the surrounding environment. Sahuarita officials subsequently clarified that the proposed site lies outside town boundaries, under Pima County jurisdiction. Project Gravel also illustrates the difficulty in determining the true size of the U.S. development pipeline. Large sites can remain in engineering, environmental and land-use review for months before appearing in conventional industry announcements. artigo.texto: Data center é desativado temporariamente na Rússia após ataques de drones da Ucrânia Drones ucranianos atingiram instalações da empresa de tecnologia russa Yandex A empresa russa de tecnologia e inteligência artificial Yandex informou que sua infraestrutura foi danificada em um ataque de drones, provocando a paralisação completa de seu data center na região de Vladimir, na região central da Rússia. Ninguém ficou ferido no ataque, mas alguns serviços da Yandex estão indisponíveis para os usuários desde domingo, informou a empresa. Em nota, a companhia disse estar restabelecendo gradualmente a prestação de serviços. Este é o terceiro grande data center a ser tirado de operação nos últimos dias. Na sexta-feira, a Yandex, que tem forte atuação no desenvolvimento de inteligência artificial na Rússia e às vezes é chamada de "Google russo", informou que seu data center na região de Kaluga, a sudoeste de Moscou, havia sido atingido por drones ucranianos e ficado parcialmente fora de operação. Um dia antes, um ataque ucraniano havia provocado a paralisação do data center da Yandex em Sasovo, a sudeste de Moscou, onde estão instalados dois dos três supercomputadores utilizados para desenvolver o modelo de inteligência artificial da empresa.

artigo.texto: Marrakech – Gotion Power Morocco (GPM) will begin commissioning and starting up the production equipment at its battery gigafactory in Kenitra during the week of October 20. The subsidiary of Chinese group Gotion High-Tech announced the schedule in a statement, describing the plant as the first of its kind in Africa and the Middle East. The startup opens the way to industrial production of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, built from lithium, iron, and phosphate, within a first phase of 20 GWh. GPM president Khalid Qalam had earlier revealed that the first cell line would begin in October, with a second line following in November. He also pointed to a start of sales for assembled batteries by the end of the year. The site sits inside the Atlantic Free Zone of Kenitra and drew MAD 13 billion ($1.3 billion) in investment for its first phase. It will produce cells and batteries for the automotive and energy storage sectors, serving the Moroccan market and the African continent, along with Europe, the Middle East, and the United States. Construction began in September 2025 after earthworks, and the buildings and infrastructure of the cell plant were completed in 13 months. According to GPM, that timeline ranks the project among the fastest industrial builds of its kind internationally. The work relied on a logistics operation of a scale new to Moroccan industry, with several thousand containers shipped from China to move production lines and high-technology equipment to Kenitra, backed by port and customs authorities. “The startup of the equipment on October 20 is only a first step in the rollout of a unique and promising project, meant to durably structure Morocco’s battery industrial ecosystem,” Qalam noted. He tied the plant to “the kingdom’s sovereignty in the field of green energy.” GPM has so far recruited more than 400 Moroccan employees, among them engineers, technicians, operators, and support staff. Most trained in China at Gotion High-Tech production sites, then worked alongside group experts in Kenitra. At full development, the gigafactory will create more than 2,300 direct jobs. The first phase targets 20 GWh of cells, battery packs, and energy storage systems, plus 100,000 tons of cathode materials. The project advanced further on September 28, when Volkswagen, a Gotion High-Tech shareholder, joined the Chinese group in announcing a Kenitra joint venture for cathode materials. That venture forms part of a broader Gotion-Volkswagen plan to invest about €3.22 billion ($3.67 billion) across battery and materials projects in Europe and North Africa, split between roughly €1.6 billion from Gotion and €1.62 billion from PowerCo, Volkswagen’s battery unit. The companies plan joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia, and Morocco, with the Kenitra cathode project set at about €480 million and 100,000 metric tons a year, prioritizing supplies to the two European battery plants. Gotion will control the Moroccan venture with a 51% stake, and PowerCo will hold 49%. Financing arrived earlier in the year. On July 24, the African Development Bank (AfDB) approved a €100 million loan to GPM for the integrated LFP gigafactory, with plans to mobilize up to €141 million more from partners. The bank described a first phase of 10 GWh scaling toward 100 GWh, and projected more than 600 direct jobs and a 70% local industrial integration rate. Gotion ranked fifth among global EV battery makers over the first seven months of 2026, with installations of 34.0 GWh, up 44.2% from a year earlier.

artigo.texto: O exército russo bombardeou dois prédios em Sloviansk e armazéns em Kiev: quatro feridos e desaparecidos sob escombros. Drones ucranianos atingem centro de dados da Yandex em Vladímir, provocando falhas, sem vítimas. Na manhã deste domingo, o exército russo atacou dois blocos de apartamentos em Sloviansk, na região de Donetsk. “Neste momento há registo de quatro feridos”, declarou o presidente da câmara da cidade, Vadym Liakh. “Todos estão a receber assistência médica”. Debaixo dos escombros poderão ainda estar pessoas, afirmou por seu lado o presidente Volodymyr Zelensky. Em Bucha, nos arredores de Kiev, um ataque russo durante a noite deixou um conjunto de armazéns de uma empresa industrial a arder. Na tarde de domingo, as equipas de bombeiros continuavam a combater o incêndio. Um paramédico e um condutor ficaram feridos depois de um drone russo atingir uma ambulância na região de Sumy. Segundo o chefe da administração militar regional, Oleg Hryhorov, os profissionais de saúde conseguiram sair sozinhos do veículo danificado. Em várias regiões da Ucrânia, devido à situação difícil no setor energético causada pelos bombardeamentos russos, foram introduzidos no domingo cortes de emergência de eletricidade, informou o serviço de imprensa da NEC “Ukrenergo”. Os horários anteriormente divulgados para cortes de eletricidade por horas estão atualmente suspensos. Os cortes de emergência serão levantados depois de estabilizada a situação no sistema energético. Drones atacam terceiro centro de dados da Yandex em Vladímir, na Rússia Drones ucranianos atacaram na noite de sábado para domingo o centro de dados da Yandex em Vladímir. A empresa informou que a infraestrutura do centro foi danificada e que a sua atividade está totalmente interrompida. Até ao momento não há registo de feridos na sequência do ataque. A Yandex acrescentou que continua a avaliar o estado da infraestrutura e que, para já, não pode indicar prazos para a reposição dos equipamentos. Este é já o terceiro centro de dados da empresa atacado em outubro. O governador Aleksandr Avdeev confirmou o ataque de drones em Vladímir e o incêndio que se seguiu. Segundo o responsável, foi possível evitar danos na zona residencial. Os moradores foram retirados das casas mais próximas do local do ataque. Em Vladímir foram desligadas duas subestações que fornecem eletricidade a 5000 residentes. Uma hora depois, o governador informou que o fornecimento de eletricidade estava restabelecido em 80% e o de aquecimento e água em 100%. Segundo dados preliminares, foi atingido um supercomputador localizado no centro de dados de Vladímir. Um equipamento idêntico está instalado no centro de dados da Yandex em Riazan, que também foi alvo de ataque. Na sequência do ataque, os utilizadores enfrentaram falhas generalizadas nos serviços da empresa. Em Moscovo, São Petersburgo, Perm, Krasnoiarsk, Vladivostoque, Ulan-Ude, Ecaterimburgo e outras cidades russas não é possível chamar táxi através da aplicação. Problemas semelhantes foram registados na Sérbia, Cazaquistão, Bielorrússia e Arménia. Motoristas referem que não conseguem entrar na aplicação ou se deparam com falhas na navegação, enquanto o serviço indica aos passageiros que não há viaturas disponíveis. Há também registo de perturbações em muitos outros serviços da empresa. A 9 de outubro, drones atacaram o centro de dados da Yandex em Kaluga. Na manhã de 8 de outubro, as Forças Armadas da Ucrânia atingiram um centro de dados da Yandex perto de Riazan. Após esses ataques, começaram falhas nos sistemas internos de grandes empresas russas. Os sites de vários grandes meios de comunicação russos também deixaram de carregar. Canais ucranianos de monitorização relatam ataques, no domingo, contra uma ponte ferroviária basculante em Rostov-do-Don. As autoridades regionais ainda não comentaram o incidente. No início de outubro, a Rússia lançou repetidos ataques contra pontes estratégicas em Kiev. Segundo revelava o jornal The Telegraph, perante reveses militares, Vladimir Putin decidiu passar a atacar infraestruturas críticas da Ucrânia e pontes em Kiev. O centro operacional da região de Krasnodar informou que “fragmentos de drones” caíram na área do aeroporto de Sochi. Um dos edifícios administrativos foi atingido por um incêndio, sem registo de feridos. Destroços caíram também em zonas residenciais. O Ministério russo da Defesa afirmou que, durante a noite, as forças de defesa antiaérea abateram 479 drones ucranianos sobre 17 regiões da Rússia e a Crimeia anexada.

JAKARTA, Oct 11 (Reuters) - Indonesian authorities and conservation workers successfully moved eight orangutans to a safe location after the endangered primates' homes were destroyed by wildfires in the forests of Borneo, they said on Sunday.
The Southeast Asian nation is battling its most intense wildfires in 11 years, mainly on Sumatra and Borneo islands, and the government has warned the blazes could continue until November, aggravated by the El Niño weather pattern.
Sign up here.
Three mother-child pairs and two adolescent male orangutans were among those rescued between August and September from several locations, the Indonesian government and wildlife foundation, Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI) said in a statement.
"Their relocation to Batu Nyambu protected forest is expected to give the eight orangutans a chance to return to living naturally," the statement read.
Orangutans are critically endangered great apes found in the wild only on the Southeast Asian islands of Borneo and Sumatra, with Indonesia home to all three recognised species, according to the World Wildlife Fund. Populations have declined due to deforestation, wildfires and poaching.
The relocation operation took six hours by car, one hour on boats, and two more hours on foot, with the orangutans in cages carried on bamboo poles. Before they were moved, YIARI conservationists checked the animals' health.
Since August, the West Kalimantan Natural Resources Conservation Agency and YIARI have rescued 46 orangutans affected by fires, agency head Murlan Dameria Pane said.
From January to July this year, fires burned around 202,000 hectares (500,000 acres) in Indonesia. No official data for subsequent months has been released, but non-governmental organisations estimate fires have burned at least 600,000 hectares more since.
Haze from the fires has caused 175,000 cases of respiratory illness in Indonesia, with the smog affecting neighbouring Singapore and Malaysia where many schools were closed on Friday as air quality deteriorated.
Reporting by Gayatri Suroyo; Editing by Gibran Peshimam and Kate Mayberry

artigo.texto: BOSTON, July 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Factorial Energy Inc.(Nasdaq: FAC) (“Factorial” or the “Company”), a global leader in next-generation solid-state battery technology, today announced it has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with SK On Co., Ltd. (“SK On”), a leading global battery manufacturer. This partnership brings together Factorial’s advanced cell technology and scale-up expertise with SK On’s extensive global manufacturing network and pilot capabilities. A key objective of this collaboration is to assess whether and how SK On’s world-class manufacturing footprint and existing lithium-ion battery manufacturing infrastructure could support future development of solid-state battery technologies. SK On is recognized as a leading global manufacturer of electric vehicle batteries serving automotive OEMs including Hyundai Motor Group, Ford, Volkswagen, and Ferrari. The company has more than 200 GWh of annual production capacity worldwide, including approximately 100 GWh in the United States. Its U.S. manufacturing footprint includes 22 GWh of capacity in Commerce, Georgia, as well as operations in Tennessee. Under the MOU, Factorial and SK On will jointly evaluate the technical feasibility and manufacturing considerations for Factorial’s FEST® solid-state battery technologies, drawing on SK On’s battery technology and manufacturing expertise, as well as its global manufacturing capabilities. The collaboration highlights Factorial’s capital-light approach to industrialization, which is centered on developing batteries that can leverage established manufacturing infrastructure to accelerate the path to industrialization. “A battery breakthrough only matters if it can be manufactured at scale,” said Siyu Huang, CEO of Factorial. “That is what makes this partnership with SK On so significant. Their manufacturing footprint spans some of the world’s most advanced battery facilities, and their expertise will be critical in shaping how solid-state battery technology integrates into global production ecosystems.” Factorial’s solid‑state platforms are engineered to serve as the core energy foundation for next‑generation mobility, aerospace systems, and hyperscale data centers. Factorial’s high energy density batteries enable smaller, lighter batteries and deliver system level efficiency required for increasingly demanding missions across land, air, and orbit. “This collaboration provides an opportunity to evaluate the technical feasibility and manufacturing readiness of solid-state battery technologies, drawing on SK On’s battery technology and manufacturing expertise,” said Ki-soo Park, Head of the Institute of Future Technology at SK On. “SK On will continue to explore collaboration opportunities in next-generation battery technologies.” Through this collaboration, Factorial and SK On will explore opportunities to support the future development of solid-state battery technologies for mobility and high-performance markets, advancing the next generation of energy storage. This marks Factorial’s manufacturing-focused partnership with a global battery producer, reflecting the company’s strategy of scaling through established manufacturing ecosystems. The MOU is non-binding, except for certain customary binding provisions. The terms of the collaboration are expected to be set forth in definitive binding agreements. About Factorial Energy Factorial Energy (Nasdaq: FAC) is a leading American solid-state battery innovator backed by IQT – the not-for-profit strategic investor for the U.S. national security community and America’s allies – and Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, Hyundai, and Kia. Through its proprietary FEST® and Solstice™ platforms, engineered for scalable manufacturing, Factorial delivers industry-leading performance across aerospace, energy storage and mobility applications. Mercedes-Benz’ real-world road testing in a lightly modified test vehicle achieved over 1,200 km of range on a single charge, while Stellantis-lab testing verified 77 Ah cells demonstrating high energy density, fast-charging, and robust use for energy and power performance across temperature extremes, with the technology successfully integrated into a fully built Dodge Charger Daytona demonstration vehicle. For more information, visit www.factorialenergy.com. About SK On SK On is a global leading battery and trading company committed to technological innovation for a better, sustainable future. SK On was launched as an independent company in October 2021 after SK Innovation, South Korea’s largest energy company, decided to split off its battery business unit. SK On aims to accelerate the green energy transition by leveraging its global production base and R&D capabilities, as well as its production and quality management know-how. Headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, SK On has a worldwide presence with battery plants currently operating or in construction across the United States, Europe, and Asia.
